And when Yahuah (God) commands the clouds to go over the whole world, they do as they are bidden.
And the fire sent from above to consume hills and woods doeth as it is commanded: but these are like to them neither in shew nor power.
Wherefore it is neither to be supposed nor said that they are gods, seeing, they are able neither to judge causes, nor to do good to men.
Knowing therefore that they are no gods, fear them not,
For they can neither curse nor bless kings:
Neither can they shew signs in the heavens among the heathen, nor shine as the sun, nor give light as the moon.
The beasts are better than they: for they can get under a cover and help themselves.
It is then by no means manifest to us that they are gods: therefore fear them not.
For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers keepeth nothing: so are their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold.
And likewise their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold, are like to a white thorn in an orchard, that every bird sits upon; as also to a dead body, that is cast into the dark.
And you shall know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rotteth upon them: and they themselves afterward shall be eaten, and shall be a reproach in the country.
Better therefore is the just man that has none idols: for he shall be far from reproach.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:1: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:2: Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:3: Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:4: Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:5: The word of Yahuah (God) most high is the fountain of wisdom; and her ways are everlasting commandments.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:6: To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? or who has known her wise counsels?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:7: To whom has the knowledge of wisdom been made manifest? and who has understood her great experience?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:8: There is one wise and greatly to be feared, Yahuah (God) sitting upon his throne.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:9: He created her, and saw her, and numbered her, and poured her out upon all his works.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:10: She is with all flesh according to his gift, and he has given her to them that love him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:11: The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:12: The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:13: Whoso fears Yahuah (God), it shall go well with him at the last, and he shall find favour in the day of his death.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:14: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:15: She has built an everlasting foundation with men, and she shall continue with their seed.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:16: To fear Yahuah (God) is fulness of wisdom, and filleth men with her fruits.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:17: She filleth all their house with things desirable, and the garners with her increase.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:18: The fear of Yahuah (God) is a crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish; both which are the gifts of Yahuah (God): and it enlargeth their rejoicing that love him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:19: Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:20: The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:21: The fear of Yahuah (God) drives away sins: and where it is present, it turns away wrath.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:22: A furious man cannot be justified; for the sway of his fury shall be his destruction.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:23: A patient man will tear for a time, and afterward joy shall spring up to him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:24: He will hide his words for a time, and the lips of many shall declare his wisdom.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:25: The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:26: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:27: For the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom and instruction: and faith and meekness are his delight.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:28: Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:29: Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|1:30: Exalt not thyself, lest you fall, and bring dishonour upon your soul, and so Yahuah (God) discover your secrets, and cast you down in the midst of the congregation, because you camest not in truth to the fear of Yahuah (God), but your heart is full of deceit.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:1: My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:2: Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:3: Cleave to him, and depart not away, that you may be increased at your last end.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:4: Whatsoever is brought upon you take cheerfully, and be patient when you are changed to a low estate.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:5: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:6: Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:7: You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:8: You that fear Yahuah (God), believe him; and your reward shall not fail.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:9: You that fear Yahuah (God), hope for good, and for everlasting joy and mercy.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:10: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:11: For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:12: Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goes two ways!
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:13: Woe to him that is fainthearted! for he believes not; therefore shall he not be defended.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:14: Woe to you that have lost patience! and what will you do when Yahuah (God) shall visit you?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:15: They that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:16: They that fear Yahuah (God) will seek that which is well, pleasing to him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:17: They that fear Yahuah (God) will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|2:18: Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:1: Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:2: For Yahuah (God) has given the father honour over the children, and has confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:3: Whoso honoureth his father makes an atonement for his sins:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:4: And he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:5: Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:6: He that honoureth his father shall have a long life; and he that is obedient to Yahuah (God) shall be a comfort to his mother.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:7: He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father, and will do service to his parents, as to his masters.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:8: Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:9: For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:10: Glory not in the dishonour of your father; for your father’s dishonour is no glory to you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:11: For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:12: My son, help your father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he lives.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:13: And if his understanding fail, have patience with him; and despise him not when you are in your full strength.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:14: For the relieving of your father shall not be forgotten: and instead of sins it shall be added to build you up.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:15: In the day of your affliction it shall be remembered; your sins also shall melt away, as the ice in the fair warm weather.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:16: He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:17: My son, go on with your business in meekness; so shall you be beloved of him that is approved.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:18: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:19: Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:20: For the power of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:21: Seek not out things that are too hard for you, neither search the things that are above your strength.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:22: But what is commanded you, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for you to see with your eyes the things that are in secret.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:23: Be not curious in unnecessary matters: for more things are shewed to you than men understand.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:24: For many are deceived by their own vain opinion; and an evil suspicion has overthrown their judgment.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:25: Without eyes you shall want light: profess not the knowledge therefore that you have not.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:26: A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loves danger shall perish in it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:27: An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrows; and the wicked man shall heap sin upon sin.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:28: In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy; for the plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:29: The heart of the prudent will understand a parable; and an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:30: Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|3:31: And he that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter; and when he falls, he shall find a stay.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:1: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:2: Make not an hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:3: Add not more trouble to an heart that is vexed; and defer not to give to him that is in need.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:4: Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:5: Turn not away your eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse you:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:6: For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:7: Get thyself the love of the congregation, and bow your head to a great man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:8: Let it not grieve you to bow down your ear to the poor, and give him a friendly answer with meekness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:9: Deliver him that suffers wrong from the hand of the oppressor; and be not fainthearted when you sittest in judgment.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:10: Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:11: Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:12: He that loves her loves life; and they that seek to her early shall be filled with joy.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:13: He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:14: They that serve her shall minister to the Holy One: and them that love her Elohim (God) does love.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:15: Whoso gives ear to her shall judge the nations: and he that attendeth to her shall dwell securely.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:16: If a man commit himself to her, he shall inherit her; and his generation shall hold her in possession.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:17: For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:18: Then will she return the straight way to him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:19: But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruin.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:20: Observe the opportunity, and beware of evil; and be not ashamed when it concerneth your soul.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:21: For there is a shame that brings sin; and there is a shame which is glory and grace.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:22: Accept no person against your soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause you to fall.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:23: And refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not your wisdom in her beauty.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:24: For by speech wisdom shall be known: and learning by the word of the tongue.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:25: In no wise speak against the truth; but be abashed of the error of your ignorance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:26: Be not ashamed to confess your sins; and force not the course of the river.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:27: Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:28: Strive for the truth to death, and Yahuah (God) shall fight for you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:29: Be not hasty in your tongue, and in your deeds slack and remiss.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:30: Be not as a lion in your house, nor frantick among your servants.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|4:31: Let not yours hand be stretched out to receive, and shut when you should repay.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:1: Set your heart upon your goods; and say not, I have enough for my life.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:2: Follow not your own mind and your strength, to walk in the ways of your heart:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:3: And say not, Who shall controul me for my works? for Yahuah (God) will surely revenge your pride.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:4: Say not, I have sinned, and what harm has happened to me? for Yahuah (God) is longsuffering, he will in no wise let you go.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:5: Concerning propitiation, be not without fear to add sin to sin:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:6: And say not His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:7: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:8: Set not yours heart upon goods unjustly gotten, for they shall not profit you in the day of calamity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:9: Winnow not with every wind, and go not into every way: for so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:10: Be stedfast in your understanding; and let your word be the same.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:11: Be swift to hear; and let your life be sincere; and with patience give answer.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:12: If you have understanding, answer your neighbour; if not, lay your hand upon your mouth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:13: Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:14: Be not called a whisperer, and lie not in wait with your tongue: for a foul shame is upon the thief, and an evil condemnation upon the double tongue.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|5:15: Be not ignorant of any thing in a great matter or a small.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:1: Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:2: Extol not thyself in the counsel of your own heart; that your soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:3: You shall eat up your leaves, and lose your fruit, and leave thyself as a dry tree.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:4: A wicked soul shall destroy him that has it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:5: Sweet language will multiply friends: and a fairspeaking tongue will increase kind greetings.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:6: Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:7: If you would get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:8: For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:9: And there is a friend, who being turned to enmity, and strife will discover your reproach.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:10: Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:11: But in your prosperity he will be as thyself, and will be bold over your servants.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:12: If you be brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himself from your face.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:13: Separate thyself from your enemies, and take heed of your friends.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:14: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:15: Nothing does countervail a faithful friend, and his excellency is invaluable.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:16: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:17: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:18: My son, gather instruction from your youth up: so shall you find wisdom till your old age.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:19: Come to her as one that ploweth and sows, and wait for her good fruits: for you shall not toil much in labouring about her, but you shall eat of her fruits right soon.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:20: She is very unpleasant to the unlearned: he that is without understanding will not remain with her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:21: She will lie upon him as a mighty stone of trial; and he will cast her from him ere it be long.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:22: For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:23: Give ear, my son, receive my advice, and refuse not my counsel,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:24: And put your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her chain.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:25: Bow down your shoulder, and bear her, and be not grieved with her bonds.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:26: Come to her with your whole heart, and keep her ways with all your power.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:27: Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you: and when you have got hold of her, let her not go.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:28: For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:29: Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for you, and her chains a robe of glory.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:30: For there is a golden ornament upon her, and her bands are purple lace.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:31: You shall put her on as a robe of honour, and shall put her about you as a crown of joy.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:32: My son, if you will, you shall be taught: and if you will apply your mind, you shall be prudent.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:33: If you love to hear, you shall receive understanding: and if you bow your ear, you shall be wise,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:34: Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave to him that is wise.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:35: Be willing to hear every godly discourse; and let not the parables of understanding escape you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:36: And if you see a man of understanding, get you betimes to him, and let your foot wear the steps of his door.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|6:37: Let your mind be upon the ordinances of Yahuah (God) and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish yours heart, and give you wisdom at your owns desire.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:1: Do no evil, so shall no harm come to you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:2: Depart from the unjust, and iniquity shall turn away from you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:3: My son, sow not upon the furrows of unrighteousness, and you shall not reap them sevenfold.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:4: Seek not of Yahuah (God) preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:5: justify not thyself before Yahuah (God); and boast not of your wisdom before the king.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:6: Seek not to be judge, being not able to take away iniquity; lest at any time you fear the person of the mighty, an stumblingblock in the way of your uprightness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:7: Offend not against the multitude of a city, and then you shall not cast thyself down among the people.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:8: Bind not one sin upon another; for in one you shall not be unpunished.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:9: Say not, Yahuah (God) will look upon the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most high Yahuah (God), he will accept it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:10: Be not fainthearted when you makest your prayer, and neglect not to give alms.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:11: Laugh no man to scorn in the bitterness of his soul: for there is one which humbleth and exalteth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:12: Devise not a lie against your brother; neither do the like to your friend.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:13: Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:14: Use not many words in a multitude of elders, and make not much babbling when you prayest.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:15: Hate not laborious work, neither husbandry, which the Most High has ordained.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:16: Number not thyself among the multitude of sinners, but remember that wrath will not tarry long.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:17: Humble thyself greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and worms.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:18: Change not a friend for any good by no means; neither a faithful brother for the gold of Ophir.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:19: Forego not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:20: Whereas your servant works truly, entreat him not evil, nor the hireling that bestoweth himself wholly for you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:21: Let your soul love a good servant, and defraud him not of liberty.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:22: Have you cattle? have an eye to them: and if they be for your profit, keep them with you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:23: Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:24: Have you daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:25: Marry your daughter, and so shall you have performed a weighty matter: but give her to a man of understanding.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:26: Have you a wife after your mind? forsake her not: but give not thyself over to a light woman.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:27: Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:28: Remember that you were begotten of them; and how can you recompense them the things that they have done for you?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:29: Fear Yahuah (God) with all your soul, and reverence his priests.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:30: Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:31: Fear Yahuah (God), and honor the priest; and give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:32: And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:33: A gift has grace in the sight of every man living; and for the dead detain it not.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:34: Fail not to be with them that weep, and mourn with them that mourn.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:35: Be not slow to visit the sick: for that shall make you to be beloved.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|7:36: Whatsoever you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amiss.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:1: Strive not with a mighty man’ lest you fall into his hands.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:2: Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he overweigh you: for gold has destroyed many, and perverted the hearts of kings.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:3: Strive not with a man that is full of tongue, and heap not wood upon his fire.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:4: Jest not with a rude man, lest your ancestors be disgraced.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:5: Reproach not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:6: Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us wax old.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:7: Rejoice not over your greatest enemy being dead, but remember that we die all.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:8: Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs: for of them you shall learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:9: Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learn understanding, and to give answer as need requires.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:10: Kindle not the coals of a sinner, lest you be burnt with the flame of his fire.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:11: Rise not up in anger at the presence of an injurious person, lest he lie in wait to entrap you in your words
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:12: Lend not to him that is mightier than thyself; for if you lendest him, count it but lost.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:13: Be not surety above your power: for if you be surety, take care to pay it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:14: Go not to law with a judge; for they will judge for him according to his honour.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:15: Travel not by the way with a bold fellow, lest he become grievous to you: for he will do according to his own will, and you shall perish with him through his folly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:16: Strive not with an angry man, and go not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no help, he will overthrow you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:17: Consult not with a fool; for he cannot keep counsel.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:18: Do no secret thing before a stranger; for you know not what he will bring forth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|8:19: Open not yours heart to every man, lest he requite you with a shrewd turn.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:1: Be not jealous over the wife of your bosom, and teach her not an evil lesson against thyself.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:2: Give not your soul to a woman to set her foot upon your substance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:3: Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:4: Use not much the company of a woman that is a singer, lest you be taken with her attempts.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:5: Gaze not on a maid, that you fall not by those things that are precious in her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:6: Give not your soul to harlots, that you lose not your inheritance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:7: Look not round about you in the streets of the city, neither wander you in the solitary place thereof.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:8: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:9: Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in your arms, and spend not your money with her at the wine; lest yours heart incline to her, and so through your desire you fall into destruction.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:10: Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:11: Envy not the glory of a sinner: for you know not what shall be his end.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:12: Delight not in the thing that the ungodly have pleasure in; but remember they shall not go unpunished to their grave.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:13: Keep you far from the man that has power to kill; so shall you not doubt the fear of death: and if you come to him, make no fault, lest he take away your life presently: remember that you go in the midst of snares, and that you walkest upon the battlements of the city.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:14: As near as you can, guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:15: Let your talk be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the Most High.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:16: And let just men eat and drink with you; and let your glorying be in the fear of Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:17: For the hand of the artificer the work shall be commended: and the wise ruler of the people for his speech.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|9:18: A man of an ill tongue is dangerous in his city; and he that is rash in his talk shall be hated.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:1: A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:2: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell in it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:3: An unwise king destroys his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:4: The power of the earth is in the hand of Yahuah (God), and in due time he will set over it one that is profitable.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:5: In the hand of Yahuah (God) is the prosperity of man: and upon the person of the scribe shall he lay his honour.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:6: Bear not hatred to your neighbour for every wrong; and do nothing at all by injurious practices.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:7: Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:8: Because of unrighteous dealings, injuries, and riches got by deceit, the kingdom is translated from one people to another.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:9: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one sets his own soul to sale; because while he lives he casteth away his bowels.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:10: The physician cutteth off a long disease; and he that is to day a king to morrow shall die.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:11: For when a man is dead, he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:12: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:13: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:14: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:15: Yahuah (God) has plucked up the roots of the proud nations, and planted the lowly in their place.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:16: Yahuah (God) overthrew countries of the heathen, and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:17: He took some of them away, and destroyed them, and has made their memorial to cease from the earth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:18: Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:19: They that fear Yahuah (God) are a sure seed, and they that love him an honourable plant: they that regard not the law are a dishonourable seed; they that transgress the commandments are a deceivable seed.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:20: Among brothers he that is chief is honorable; so are they that fear Yahuah (God) in his eyes.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:21: The fear of Yahuah (God) goes before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:22: Whether he be rich, noble, or poor, their glory is the fear of Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:23: It is not meet to despise the poor man that has understanding; neither is it convenient to magnify a sinful man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:24: Great men, and judges, and potentates, shall be honoured; yet is there none of them greater than he that fears Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:25: To the servant that is wise shall they that are free do service: and he that has knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:26: Be not overwise in doing your business; and boast not thyself in the time of your distress.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:27: Better is he that laboureth, and abounds in all things, than he that boasteth himself, and wanteth bread.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:28: My son, glorify your soul in meekness, and give it honour according to the dignity thereof.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:29: Who will justify him that sinneth against his own soul? and who will honour him that dishonoureth his own life?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:30: The poor man is honoured for his skill, and the rich man is honoured for his riches.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|10:31: He that is honoured in poverty, how much more in riches? and he that is dishonourable in riches, how much more in poverty?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:1: Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and makes him to sit among great men.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:2: Commend not a man for his beauty; neither abhor a man for his outward appearance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:3: The bee is little among such as fly; but her fruit is the chief of sweet things.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:4: Boast not of your clothing and raiment, and exalt not thyself in the day of honour: for the works of Yahuah (God) are wonderful, and his works among men are hidden.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:5: Many kings have sat down upon the ground; and one that was never thought of has worn the crown.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:6: Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced; and the honourable delivered into other men’s hands.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:7: Blame not before you have examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:8: Answer not before you have heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talk.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:9: Strive not in a matter that concerneth you not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:10: My son, meddle not with many matters: for if you meddle much, you shall not be innocent; and if you follow after, you shall not obtain, neither shall you escape by fleeing.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:11: There is one that laboureth, and takes pains, and makes haste, and is so much the more behind.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:12: Again, there is another that is slow, and has need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty; yet the eye of Yahuah (God) looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:13: And lifted up his head from misery; so that many that saw it marvelled at him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:14: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:15: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding of the law, are of Yahuah (God): love, and the way of good works, are from him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:16: Error and darkness had their beginning together with sinners: and evil shall wax old with them that glory in it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:17: The gift of Yahuah (God) remains with the ungodly, and his favour brings prosperity for ever.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:18: There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:19: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:20: Be stedfast in your covenant, and be conversant in it, and wax old in your work.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:21: Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:22: The blessing of Yahuah (God) is in the reward of the godly, and suddenly he makes his blessing flourish.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:23: Say not, What profit is there of my service? and what good things shall I have hereafter?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:24: Again, say not, I have enough, and possess many things, and what evil shall I have hereafter?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:25: In the day of prosperity there is a forgetfulness of affliction: and in the day of affliction there is no more remembrance of prosperity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:26: For it is an easy thing to Yahuah (God) in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:27: The affliction of an hour makes a man forget pleasure: and in his end his deeds shall be discovered.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:28: Judge none blessed before his death: for a man shall be known in his children.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:29: Bring not every man into yours house: for the deceitful man has many trains.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:30: Like as a partridge taken and kept in a cage, so is the heart of the proud; and like as a spy, watcheth he for your fall:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:31: For he lieth in wait, and turns good into evil, and in things worthy praise will lay blame upon you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:32: Of a spark of fire a heap of coals is kindled: and a sinful man layeth wait for blood.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:33: Take heed of a mischievous man, for he works wickedness; lest he bring upon you a perpetual blot.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|11:34: Receive a stranger into yours house, and he will disturb you, and turn you out of your own.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:1: When you will do good know to whom you do it; so shall you be thanked for your benefits.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:2: Do good to the godly man, and you shall find a recompence; and if not from him, yet from the Most High.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:3: There can no good come to him that is always occupied in evil, nor to him that gives no alms.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:4: Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:5: Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby: for else you shall receive twice as much evil for all the good you shall have done to him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:6: For the Most High hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly, and keepeth them against the mighty day of their punishment.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:7: Give to the good, and help not the sinner.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:8: A friend cannot be known in prosperity: and an enemy cannot be hidden in adversity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:9: In the prosperity of a man enemies will be grieved: but in his adversity even a friend will depart.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:10: Never trust your enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:11: Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him, and you shall be to him as if you had wiped a lookingglass, and you shall know that his rust has not been altogether wiped away.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:12: Set him not by you, lest, when he has overthrown you, he stand up in your place; neither let him sit at your right hand, lest he seek to take your seat, and you at the last remember my words, and be pricked with it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:13: Who will pity a charmer that is bitten with a serpent, or any such as come nigh wild beasts?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:14: So one that goes to a sinner, and is defiled with him in his sins, who will pity?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:15: For a while he will abide with you, but if you begin to fall, he will not tarry.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:16: An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit: he will weep with his eyes, but if he find opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:17: If adversity come upon you, you shall find him there first; and though he pretend to help you, yet shall he undermine you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|12:18: He will shake his head, and clap his hands, and whisper much, and change his countenance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:1: He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled with it; and he that has fellowship with a proud man shall be like to him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:2: Burden not thyself above your power while you livest; and have no fellowship with one that is mightier and richer than thyself: for how agree the kettle and the earthen pot together? for if the one be struck against the other, it shall be broken.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:3: The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threateneth withal: the poor is wronged, and he must intreat also.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:4: If you be for his profit, he will use you: but if you have nothing, he will forsake you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:5: If you have any thing, he will live with you: yes, he will make you bare, and will not be sorry for it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:6: If he have need of you, he will deceive you, and smile upon you, and put you in hope; he will speak you fair, and say, What wantest you?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:7: And he will shame you by his meats, until he have drawn you dry twice or thrice, and at the last he will laugh you to scorn afterward, when he seeth you, he will forsake you, and shake his head at you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:8: Beware that you be not deceived and brought down in your jollity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:9: If you be invited of a mighty man, withdraw thyself, and so much the more will he invite you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:10: Press you not upon him, lest you be put back; stand not far off, lest you be forgotten.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:11: Affect not to be made equal to him in talk, and believe not his many words: for with much communication will he tempt you, and smiling upon you will get out your secrets:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:12: But cruelly he will lay up your words, and will not spare to do you hurt, and to put you in prison.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:13: Observe, and take good heed, for you walkest in peril of your overthrowing: when you hear these things, awake in your sleep.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:14: Love Yahuah (God) all your life, and call upon him for your salvation.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:15: Every beast loves his like, and every man loves his neighbor.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:16: All flesh consorteth according to kind, and a man will cleave to his like.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:17: What fellowship has the wolf with the lamb? so the sinner with the godly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:18: What agreement is there between the hyena and a dog? and what peace between the rich and the poor?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:19: As the wild ass is the lion’s prey in the wilderness: so the rich eat up the poor.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:20: As the proud hate humility: so does the rich abhor the poor.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:21: A rich man beginning to fall is held up of his friends: but a poor man being down is thrust away by his friends.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:22: When a rich man is fallen, he has many helpers: he speaks things not to be spoken, and yet men justify him: the poor man slipped, and yet they rebuked him too; he spoke wisely, and could have no place.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:23: When a rich man speaks, every man holdeth his tongue, and, look, what he says, they extol it to the clouds: but if the poor man speak, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will help to overthrow him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:24: Riches are good to him that has no sin, and poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:25: The heart of a man changeth his countenance, whether it be for good or evil: and a merry heart makes a cheerful countenance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|13:26: A cheerful countenance is a token of a heart that is in prosperity; and the finding out of parables is a wearisome labour of the mind.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:1: Blessed is the man that has not slipped with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sins.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:2: Blessed is he whose conscience has not condemned him, and who is not fallen from his hope in Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:3: Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an envious man do with money?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:4: He that gathers by defrauding his own soul gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:5: He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? he shall not take pleasure in his goods.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:6: There is none worse than he that envies himself; and this is a recompence of his wickedness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:7: And if he doeth good, he doeth it unwillingly; and at the last he will declare his wickedness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:8: The envious man has a wicked eye; he turns away his face, and despiseth men.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:9: A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:10: A wicked eye envies his bread, and he is a niggard at his table.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:11: My son, according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:12: Remember that death will not be long in coming, and that the covenant of the grave is not shewed to you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:13: Do good to your friend before you die, and according to your ability stretch out your hand and give to him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:14: Defraud not thyself of the good day, and let not the part of a good desire overpass you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:15: Shall you not leave your travails to another? and your labours to be divided by lot?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:16: Give, and take, and sanctify your soul; for there is no seeking of dainties in the grave.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:17: All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:18: As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one comes to an end, and another is born.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:19: Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:20: Blessed is the man that does meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:21: He that considereth her ways in his heart shall also have understanding in her secrets.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:22: Go after her as one that traceth, and lie in wait in her ways.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:23: He that prieth in at her windows shall also hearken at her doors.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:24: He that does lodge near her house shall also fasten a pin in her walls.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:25: He shall pitch his tent nigh to her, and shall lodge in a lodging where good things are.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:26: He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|14:27: By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:1: He that fears Yahuah (God) will do good, and he that has the knowledge of the law shall obtain her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:2: And as a mother shall she meet him, and receive him as a wife married of a virgin.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:3: With the bread of understanding shall she feed him, and give him the water of wisdom to drink.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:4: He shall be stayed upon her, and shall not be moved; and shall rely upon her, and shall not be confounded.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:5: She shall exalt him above his neighbours, and in the midst of the congregation shall she open his mouth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:6: He shall find joy and a crown of gladness, and she shall cause him to inherit an everlasting name.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:7: But foolish men shall not attain to her, and sinners shall not see her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:8: For she is far from pride, and men that are liars cannot remember her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:9: Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent him of Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:10: For praise shall be uttered in wisdom, and Yahuah (God) will prosper it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:11: Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:12: Say not you, He has caused me to err: for he has no need of the sinful man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:13: Yahuah (God) hates all abomination; and they that fear Yahuah (God) love it not.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:14: He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel;
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:15: If you will, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:16: He has set fire and water before you: stretch forth your hand to whether you will.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:17: Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:18: For the wisdom of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:19: And his eyes are upon them that fear him, and he knoweth every work of man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|15:20: He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:1: Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:2: Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of Yahuah (God) be with them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:3: Trust not you in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:4: For by one that has understanding shall the city be replenished: but the kindred of the wicked shall speedily become desolate.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:5: Many such things have I seen with my eyes, and my ear has heard greater things than these.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:6: In the congregation of the ungodly shall a fire be kindled; and in a rebellious nation wrath is set on fire.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:7: He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:8: Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:9: He pitied not the people of perdition, who were taken away in their sins:
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:10: Nor the six hundred thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:11: And if there be one stiffnecked among the people, it is marvel if he escape unpunished: for mercy and wrath are with him; he is mighty to forgive, and to pour out displeasure.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:12: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judges a man according to his works
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:13: The sinner shall not escape with his spoils: and the patience of the godly shall not be frustrate.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:14: Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:15: Yahuah (God) hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:16: His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he has separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:17: Say not you, I will hide myself from Yahuah (God): shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:18: Behold, the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, the deep, and the earth, and all that in it is, shall be moved when he shall visit.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:19: The mountains also and foundations of the earth be shaken with trembling, when Yahuah (God) looketh upon them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:20: No heart can think upon these things worthily: and who is able to conceive his ways?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:21: It is a tempest which no man can see: for the most part of his works are hid.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:22: Who can declare the works of his justice? or who can endure them? for his covenant is afar off, and the trial of all things is in the end.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:23: He that wanteth understanding will think upon vain things: and a foolish man erring imagineth follies.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:24: My son, hearken to me, and learn knowledge, and mark my words with your heart.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:25: I will shew forth doctrine in weight, and declare his knowledge exactly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:26: The works of Yahuah (God) are done in judgment from the beginning: and from the time he made them he disposed the parts thereof.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:27: He garnished his works for ever, and in his hand are the chief of them to all generations: they neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their works.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:28: None of them hindereth another, and they shall never disobey his word.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:29: After this Yahuah (God) looked upon the earth, and filled it with his blessings.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|16:30: With all manner of living things has he covered the face thereof; and they shall return into it again.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:1: Yahuah (God) created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:2: He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things in it.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:3: He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:4: And put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:5: They received the use of the five operations of Yahuah (God), and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:6: Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:7: Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:8: He set his eye upon their hearts, that he might shew them the greatness of his works.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:9: He gave them to glory in his marvellous acts for ever, that they might declare his works with understanding.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:10: And the elect shall praise his holy name.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:11: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:12: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:13: Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory, and their ears heard his glorious voice.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:14: And he said to them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:15: Their ways are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:16: Every man from his youth is given to evil; neither could they make to themselves fleshy hearts for stony.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:17: For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Yashar'el (Israel) is the portion of Yahuah (God):
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:18: Whom, being his firstborn, he nourishes with discipline, and giving him the light of his love does not forsake him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:19: Therefore all their works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon their ways.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:20: None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sins are before Yahuah (God)
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:21: But Yahuah (God) being gracious and knowing his workmanship, neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:22: The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deeds of man as the apple of the eye, and give repentance to his sons and daughters.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:23: Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:24: But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:25: Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:26: Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:27: Who shall praise the Most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:28: Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart shall praise Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:29: How great is the lovingkindness of Yahuah (God), our Elohim (God), and his compassion to such as turn to him in holiness!
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:30: For all things cannot be in men, because the son of Adam is not immortal.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:31: What is brighter than the sun? yet the light thereof fails; and flesh and blood will imagine evil.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|17:32: He vieweth the power of the height of heaven; and all men are but earth and ashes.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:1: He that lives for ever Has created all things in general.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:2: Yahuah (God) only is righteous, and there is none other but he,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:3: Who governeth the world with the palm of his hand, and all things obey his will: for he is the King of all, by his power dividing holy things among them from profane.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:4: To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:5: Who shall number the strength of his majesty? and who shall also tell out his mercies?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:6: As for the wondrous works of Yahuah (God), there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:7: When a man has done, then he begins; and when he leaveth off, then he shall be doubtful.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:8: What is man, and to which serveth he? what is his good, and what is his evil?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:9: The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:10: As a drop of water to the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:11: Therefore is Yahuah (God) patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:12: He saw and perceived their end to be evil; therefore he multiplied his compassion.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:13: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:14: He has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:15: My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when you give any thing.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:16: Shall not the dew asswage the heat? so is a word better than a gift.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:17: Lo, is not a word better than a gift? but both are with a gracious man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:18: A fool will upbraid churlishly, and a gift of the envious consumeth the eyes.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:19: Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:20: Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation you shall find mercy.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:21: Humble thyself before you be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:22: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:23: Before you prayest, prepare thyself; and be not as one that tempteth Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:24: Think upon the wrath that shall be at the end, and the time of vengeance, when he shall turn away his face.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:25: When you have enough, remember the time of hunger: and when you are rich, think upon poverty and need.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:26: From the morning until the evening the time is changed, and all things are soon done before Yahuah (God).
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:27: A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a fool will not observe time.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:28: Every man of understanding knoweth wisdom, and will give praise to him that found her.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:29: They that were of understanding in sayings became also wise themselves, and poured forth exquisite parables.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:30: Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:31: If you give your soul the desires that please her, she will make you a laughingstock to your enemies that malign you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:32: Take not pleasure in much good cheer, neither be tied to the expence thereof.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|18:33: Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when you have nothing in your purse: for you shall lie in wait for your own life, and be talked on.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:1: A labouring man that is given to drunkenness shall not be rich: and he that contemneth small things shall fall by little and little.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:2: Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:3: Moths and worms shall have him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:4: He that is hasty to give credit is lightminded; and he that sinneth shall offend against his own soul.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:5: Whoso takes pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:6: He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife; and he that hates babbling shall have less evil.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:7: Rehearse not to another that which is told to you, and you shall fare never the worse.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:8: Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men’s lives; and if you can without offence, reveal them not.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:9: For he heard and observed you, and when time comes he will hate you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:10: If you have heard a word, let it die with you; and be bold, it will not burst you.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:11: A fool travaileth with a word, as a woman in labour of a child.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:12: As an arrow that sticketh in a man’s thigh, so is a word within a fool’s belly.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:13: Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:14: Admonish your friend, it may be he has not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:15: Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:16: There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that has not offended with his tongue?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:17: Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the Most High.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:18: The fear of Yahuah (God) is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:19: The knowledge of the commandments of Yahuah (God) is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:20: The fear of Yahuah (God) is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:21: If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth you; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourishes him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:22: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:23: There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination; and there is a fool wanting in wisdom.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:24: He that has small understanding, and fears Yahuah (God), is better than one that has much wisdom, and transgresseth the law of the Most High.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:25: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turns aside to make judgment appear; and there is a wise man that justifies in judgment.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:26: There is a wicked man that hangeth down his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit,
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:27: Casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not known, he will do you a mischief before you be aware.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:28: And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he finds opportunity he will do evil.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:29: A man may be known by his look, and one that has understanding by his countenance, when you meetest him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|19:30: A man’s attire, and excessive laughter, and gait, shew what he is.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:1: There is a reproof that is not comely: again, some man holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:2: It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:3: How good is it, when you are reproved, to shew repentance! for so shall you escape wilful sin.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:4: As is the lust of an eunuch to deflower a virgin; so is he that executeth judgment with violence.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:5: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:6: Some man holdeth his tongue, because he has not to answer: and some keepeth silence, knowing his time.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:7: A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:8: He that useth many words shall be abhorred; and he that takes to himself authority in it shall be hated.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:9: There is a sinner that has good success in evil things; and there is a gain that turns to loss.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:10: There is a gift that shall not profit you; and there is a gift whose recompence is double.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:11: There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifteth up his head from a low estate.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:12: There is that buyeth much for a little, and repayeth it sevenfold.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:13: A wise man by his words makes him beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:14: The gift of a fool shall do you no good when you have it; neither yet of the envious for his necessity: for he looketh to receive many things for one.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:15: He gives little, and upbraideth much; he opens his mouth like a crier; to day he lendeth, and to morrow will he ask it again: such an one is to be hated of Yahuah (God) and man.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:16: The fool says, I have no friends, I have no thank for all my good deeds, and they that eat my bread speak evil of me.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:17: How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorn! for he knoweth not aright what it is to have; and it is all one to him as if he had it not.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:18: To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:19: An unseasonable tale will always be in the mouth of the unwise.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:20: A wise sentence shall be rejected when it comes out of a fool’s mouth; for he will not speak it in due season.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:21: There is that is hindered from sinning through want: and when he takes rest, he shall not be troubled.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:22: There is that destroys his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:23: There is that for bashfulness promiseth to his friend, and makes him his enemy for nothing.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:24: A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:25: A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:26: The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:27: A wise man shall promote himself to honour with his words: and he that has understanding will please great men.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:28: He that tilleth his land shall increase his heap: and he that pleaseth great men shall get pardon for iniquity.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:29: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:30: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:31: Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|20:32: Necessary patience in seeking Yahuah (God) is better than he that leadeth his life without a guide.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:1: My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:2: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if you come too near it, it will bite you: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:3: All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds of which cannot be healed.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:4: To terrify and do wrong will waste riches: thus the house of proud men shall be made desolate.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:5: A prayer out of a poor man’s mouth reacheth to the ears of Yahuah (God), and his judgment comes speedily.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:6: He that hates to be reproved is in the way of sinners: but he that fears Yahuah (God) will repent from his heart.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:7: An eloquent man is known far and near; but a man of understanding knoweth when he slippeth.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:8: He that buildeth his house with other men’s money is like one that gathers himself stones for the tomb of his burial.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:9: The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:10: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:11: He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:12: He that is not wise will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:13: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsel is like a pure fountain of life.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:14: The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:15: If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add to it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:16: The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:17: They enquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:18: As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as talk without sense.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:19: Doctrine to fools is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:20: A fool lifteth up his voice with laughter; but a wise man does scarce smile a little.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:21: Learning is to a wise man as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arm.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:22: A foolish man’s foot is soon in his neighbour’s house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:23: A fool will peep in at the door into the house: but he that is well nurtured will stand without.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:24: It is the rudeness of a man to hearken at the door: but a wise man will be grieved with the disgrace.
live.apocrypha|ecclesiasticus|21:25: The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertain not to them: but the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance.
