live.canon|1-samuel|18:11: And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it. And David avoided out of his presence twice.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:12: And Saul was afraid of David, because Yahuah (LORD) was with him, and was departed from Saul.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:13: Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:14: And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and Yahuah (LORD) was with him.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:15: Wherefore when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he was afraid of him.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:16: But all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah) loved David, because he went out and came in before them.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:18: And David said unto Saul, Who am I? and what is my life, or my father’s family in Yashar'el (Israel), that I should be son in law to the king?
live.canon|1-samuel|18:19: But it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul’s daughter should have been given to David, that she was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:20: And Michal Saul’s daughter loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:24: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, On this manner spake David.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:26: And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king’s son in law: and the days were not expired.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:27: Wherefore David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full tale to the king, that he might be the king’s son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:28: And Saul saw and knew that Yahuah (LORD) was with David, and that Michal Saul’s daughter loved him.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:29: And Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul became David’s enemy continually.
live.canon|1-samuel|18:30: Then the princes of the Philistines went forth: and it came to pass, after they went forth, that David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was much set by.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:2: But Jonathan Saul’s son delighted much in David: and Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeks to kill you: now therefore, I pray you, take heed to thyself until the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself:
live.canon|1-samuel|19:3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will commune with my father of you; and what I see, that I will tell you.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:4: And Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father, and said unto him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he has not sinned against you, and because his works have been to you-ward very good:
live.canon|1-samuel|19:5: For he did put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine, and Yahuah (LORD) wrought a great salvation for all Yashar'el (Israel): you saw it, and did rejoice: wherefore then will you sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?
live.canon|1-samuel|19:6: And Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, As Yahuah (LORD) lives, he shall not be slain.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:11: Saul also sent messengers unto David’s house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal David’s wife told him, saying, If you save not your life to night, to morrow you shall be slain.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:17: And Saul said unto Michal, Why have you deceived me so, and sent away my enemy, that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go; why should I kill you?
live.canon|1-samuel|19:1: And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:7: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan shewed him all those things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as in times past.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:8: And there was war again: and David went out, and fought with the Philistines, and slew them with a great slaughter; and they fled from him.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:9: And the evil spirit from Yahuah (LORD) was upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his javelin in his hand: and David played with his hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:10: And Saul sought to smite David even to the wall with the javelin; but he slipped away out of Saul’s presence, and he smote the javelin into the wall: and David fled, and escaped that night.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:12: So Michal let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:13: And Michal took an image, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster, and covered it with a cloth.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:14: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He is sick.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:15: And Saul sent the messengers again to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:16: And when the messengers were come in, behold, there was an image in the bed, with a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:18: So David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:19: And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:20: And Saul sent messengers to take David: and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as appointed over them, the Spirit of Elohim (God) was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:21: And when it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they prophesied also.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:22: Then went he also to Ramah, and came to a great well that is in Sechu: and he asked and said, Where are Samuel and David? And one said, Behold, they be at Naioth in Ramah.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:23: And he went thither to Naioth in Ramah: and the Spirit of Elohim (God) was upon him also, and he went on, and prophesied, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
live.canon|1-samuel|19:24: And he stripped off his clothes also, and prophesied before Samuel in like manner, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:1: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? what is my iniquity? and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:2: And he said unto him, Elohim (God) forbid; you shall not die: behold, my father will do nothing either great or small, but that he will shew it me: and why should my father hide this thing from me? it is not so.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:3: And David sware moreover, and said, Your father certainly knows that I have found grace in your eyes; and he says, Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved: but truly as Yahuah (LORD) lives, and as your soul lives, there is but a step between me and death.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:6: If your father at all miss me, then say, David earnestly asked leave of me that he might run to Beth-lehem his city: for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:7: If he say thus, It is well; your servant shall have peace: but if he be very wroth, then be sure that evil is determined by him.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:8: Therefore you shall deal kindly with your servant; for you have brought your servant into a covenant of Yahuah (LORD) with you: notwithstanding, if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for why should you bring me to your father?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:9: And Jonathan said, Far be it from you: for if I knew certainly that evil were determined by my father to come upon you, then would not I tell it you?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:10: Then said David to Jonathan, Who shall tell me? or what if your father answer you roughly?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:12: And Jonathan said unto David, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), when I have sounded my father about to morrow any time, or the third day, and, behold, if there be good toward David, and I then send not unto you, and shew it you;
live.canon|1-samuel|20:13: Yahuah (LORD) do so and much more to Jonathan: but if it please my father to do you evil, then I will shew it you, and send you away, that you may go in peace: and Yahuah (LORD) be with you, as he has been with my father.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:14: And you shall not only while yet I live shew me the kindness of Yahuah (LORD), that I die not:
live.canon|1-samuel|20:15: But also you shall not cut off your kindness from my house for ever: no, not when Yahuah (LORD) has cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:18: Then Jonathan said to David, To morrow is the new moon: and you shall be missed, because your seat will be empty.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:19: And when you have stayed three days, then you shall go down quickly, and come to the place where you did hide thyself when the business was in hand, and shall remain by the stone Ezel.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:21: And, behold, I will send a lad, saying, Go, find out the arrows. If I expressly say unto the lad, Behold, the arrows are on this side of you, take them; then come you: for there is peace to you, and no hurt; as Yahuah (LORD) lives.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:22: But if I say thus unto the young man, Behold, the arrows are beyond you; go your way: for Yahuah (LORD) has sent you away.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:23: And as touching the matter which you and I have spoken of, behold, Yahuah (LORD) be between you and me for ever.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:26: Nevertheless Saul spake not any thing that day: for he thought, Something has befallen him, he is not clean; surely he is not clean.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:27: And it came to pass on the morrow, which was the second day of the month, that David’s place was empty: and Saul said unto Jonathan his son, Wherefore comes not the son of Jesse to meat, neither yesterday, nor to day?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:29: And he said, Let me go, I pray you; for our family has a sacrifice in the city; and my brother, he has commanded me to be there: and now, if I have found favour in your eyes, let me get away, I pray you, and see my brethren. Therefore he comes not unto the king’s table.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:30: Then Saul’s anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him, You son of the perverse rebellious woman, do not I know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own confusion, and unto the confusion of your mother’s nakedness?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:31: For as long as the son of Jesse lives upon the ground, you shall not be established, nor your kingdom. Wherefore now send and fetch him unto me, for he shall surely die.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:32: And Jonathan answered Saul his father, and said unto him, Wherefore shall he be slain? what has he done?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:37: And when the lad was come to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried after the lad, and said, Is not the arrow beyond you?
live.canon|1-samuel|20:42: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of Yahuah (LORD), saying, Yahuah (LORD) be between me and you, and between my seed and your seed for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:5: And David said unto Jonathan, Behold, to morrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit with the king at meat: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field unto the third day at even.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:11: And Jonathan said unto David, Come, and let us go out into the field. And they went out both of them into the field.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:16: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, Let Yahuah (LORD) even require it at the hand of David’s enemies.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:17: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:20: And I will shoot three arrows on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:24: So David hid himself in the field: and when the new moon was come, the king sat him down to eat meat.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:25: And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, even upon a seat by the wall: and Jonathan arose, and Abner sat by Saul’s side, and David’s place was empty.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:4: Then said Jonathan unto David, Whatsoever your soul desires, I will even do it for you.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:28: And Jonathan answered Saul, David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Beth-lehem:
live.canon|1-samuel|20:33: And Saul cast a javelin at him to smite him: whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:34: So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and did eat no meat the second day of the month: for he was grieved for David, because his father had done him shame.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:35: And it came to pass in the morning, that Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a little lad with him.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:36: And he said unto his lad, Run, find out now the arrows which I shoot. And as the lad ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:38: And Jonathan cried after the lad, Make speed, haste, stay not. And Jonathan’s lad gathered up the arrows, and came to his master.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:39: But the lad knew not any thing: only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:40: And Jonathan gave his artillery unto his lad, and said unto him, Go, carry them to the city.
live.canon|1-samuel|20:41: And as soon as the lad was gone, David arose out of a place toward the south, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed himself three times: and they kissed one another, and wept one with another, until David exceeded.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:1: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech was afraid at the meeting of David, and said unto him, Why are you alone, and no man with you?
live.canon|1-samuel|21:2: And David said unto Ahimelech the priest, The king has commanded me a business, and has said unto me, Let no man know any thing of the business whereabout I send you, and what I have commanded you: and I have appointed my servants to such and such a place.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:3: Now therefore what is under your hand? give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or what there is present.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:4: And the priest answered David, and said, There is no common bread under my hand, but there is hallowed bread; if the young men have kept themselves at least from women.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:8: And David said unto Ahimelech, And is there not here under your hand spear or sword? for I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:9: And the priest said, The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you slewest in the valley of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod: if you will take that, take it: for there is no other save that here. And David said, There is none like that; give it me.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:11: And the servants of Achish said unto him, Is not this David the king of the land? did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying, Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
live.canon|1-samuel|21:14: Then said Achish unto his servants, Lo, you see the man is mad: wherefore then have you brought him to me?
live.canon|1-samuel|21:15: Have I need of mad men, that you have brought this fellow to play the mad man in my presence? shall this fellow come into my house?
live.canon|1-samuel|21:5: And David answered the priest, and said unto him, Of a truth women have been kept from us about these three days, since I came out, and the vessels of the young men are holy, and the bread is in a manner common, yea, though it were sanctified this day in the vessel.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:6: So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before Yahuah (LORD), to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:7: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before Yahuah (LORD); and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:10: And David arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:12: And David laid up these words in his heart, and was sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
live.canon|1-samuel|21:13: And he changed his behaviour before them, and feigned himself mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down upon his beard.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:3: And David went thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said unto the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray you, come forth, and be with you, till I know what Elohim (God) will do for me.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:5: And the prophet Gad said unto David, Abide not in the hold; depart, and get you into the land of Yahudah (Judah). Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hareth.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:7: Then Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear now, you Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds;
live.canon|1-samuel|22:8: That all of you have conspired against me, and there is none that shows me that my son has made a league with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or shows unto me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
live.canon|1-samuel|22:13: And Saul said unto him, Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread, and a sword, and have enquired of Elohim (God) for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
live.canon|1-samuel|22:14: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all your servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goes at your bidding, and is honourable in your house?
live.canon|1-samuel|22:15: Did I then begin to enquire of Elohim (God) for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for your servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:18: And the king said to Doeg, Turn you, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:22: And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of your father’s house.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:23: Abide you with me, fear not: for he that seeks my life seeks your life: but with me you shall be in safeguard.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:1: David therefore departed thence, and escaped to the cave Adullam: and when his brethren and all his father’s house heard it, they went down thither to him.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:2: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:4: And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they dwelt with him all the while that David was in the hold.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:6: When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him, (now Saul abode in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;)
live.canon|1-samuel|22:9: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:12: And Saul said, Hear now, you son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:10: And he enquired of Yahuah (LORD) for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:11: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:17: And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of Yahuah (LORD); because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of Yahuah (LORD).
live.canon|1-samuel|22:19: And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:20: And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:21: And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the LORD’S priests.
live.canon|1-samuel|22:16: And the king said, You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you, and all your father’s house.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:4: Then David enquired of Yahuah (LORD) yet again. And Yahuah (LORD) answered him and said, Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:7: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keilah. And Saul said, Elohim (God) has delivered him into my hand; for he is shut in, by entering into a town that has gates and bars.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:10: Then said David, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), your servant has certainly heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:11: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), I beseech you, tell your servant. And Yahuah (LORD) said, He will come down.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:12: Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul? And Yahuah (LORD) said, They will deliver you up.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:17: And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you; and you shall be king over Yashar'el (Israel), and I shall be next unto you; and that also Saul my father knows.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:19: Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Does not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?
live.canon|1-samuel|23:20: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:21: And Saul said, Blessed be you of Yahuah (LORD); for you have compassion on me.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:22: Go, I pray you, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there: for it is told me that he deals very subtilly.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:23: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides himself, and come you again to me with the certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Yahudah (Judah).
live.canon|1-samuel|23:27: But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste you, and come; for the Philistines have invaded the land.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:1: Then they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines fight against Keilah, and they rob the threshingfloors.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:2: Therefore David enquired of Yahuah (LORD), saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And Yahuah (LORD) said unto David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:3: And David’s men said unto him, Behold, we be afraid here in Yahudah (Judah): how much more then if we come to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?
live.canon|1-samuel|23:5: So David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:6: And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:8: And Saul called all the people together to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:9: And David knew that Saul secretly practised mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring hither the ephod.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:13: Then David and his men, which were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go. And it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah; and he forbare to go forth.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:14: And David abode in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but Elohim (God) delivered him not into his hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:15: And David saw that Saul was come out to seek his life: and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:16: And Jonathan Saul’s son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in Elohim (God).
live.canon|1-samuel|23:18: And they two made a covenant before Yahuah (LORD): and David abode in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:24: And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:25: Saul also and his men went to seek him. And they told David: wherefore he came down into a rock, and abode in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:26: And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:28: Wherefore Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth.
live.canon|1-samuel|23:29: And David went up from thence, and dwelt in strong holds at En-gedi.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:4: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which Yahuah (LORD) said unto you, Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do to him as it shall seem good unto you. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:6: And he said unto his men, Yahuah (LORD) forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD’S anointed, to stretch forth my hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of Yahuah (LORD).
live.canon|1-samuel|24:9: And David said to Saul, Wherefore hear you men’s words, saying, Behold, David seeks your hurt?
live.canon|1-samuel|24:10: Behold, this day your eyes have seen how that Yahuah (LORD) had delivered you to day into my hand in the cave: and some bade me kill you: but my eye spared you; and I said, I will not put forth my hand against my lord; for he is the LORD’S anointed.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:11: Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of your robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe, and killed you not, know you and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you; yet you huntest my soul to take it.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:12: Yahuah (LORD) judge between me and you, and Yahuah (LORD) avenge me of you: but my hand shall not be upon you.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:13: As says the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceeds from the wicked: but my hand shall not be upon you.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:14: After whom is the king of Yashar'el (Israel) come out? after whom do you pursue? after a dead dog, after a flea.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:15: Yahuah (LORD) therefore be judge, and judge between me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of your hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:16: And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this your voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:17: And he said to David, You are more righteous than I: for you have rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded you evil.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:18: And you have shewed this day how that you have dealt well with me: forasmuch as when Yahuah (LORD) had delivered me into your hand, you killedst me not.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:19: For if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away? wherefore Yahuah (LORD) reward you good for that you have done unto me this day.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:20: And now, behold, I know well that you shall surely be king, and that the kingdom of Yashar'el (Israel) shall be established in your hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:21: Swear now therefore unto me by Yahuah (LORD), that you will not cut off my seed after me, and that you will not destroy my name out of my father’s house.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:1: And it came to pass, when Saul was returned from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:2: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Yashar'el (Israel), and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:3: And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:5: And it came to pass afterward, that David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:7: So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. But Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:8: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself.
live.canon|1-samuel|24:22: And David sware unto Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men gat them up unto the hold.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:6: And thus shall you say to him that lives in prosperity, Peace be both to you, and peace be to your house, and peace be unto all that you have.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:7: And now I have heard that you have shearers: now your shepherds which were with us, we hurt them not, neither was there ought missing unto them, all the while they were in Carmel.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:8: Ask your young men, and they will shew you. Wherefore let the young men find favour in your eyes: for we come in a good day: give, I pray you, whatsoever comes to your hand unto your servants, and to your son David.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:13: And David said unto his men, Gird you on every man his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred abode by the stuff.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:17: Now therefore know and consider what you will do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he is such a son of Belial, that a man cannot speak to him.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:21: Now David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained unto him: and he has requited me evil for good.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:24: And fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be: and let your handmaid, I pray you, speak in your audience, and hear the words of your handmaid.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:25: Let not my lord, I pray you, regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I your handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom you did send.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:26: Now therefore, my lord, as Yahuah (LORD) lives, and as your soul lives, seeing Yahuah (LORD) has withholden you from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with your own hand, now let your enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:27: And now this blessing which your handmaid has brought unto my lord, let it even be given unto the young men that follow my lord.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:28: I pray you, forgive the trespass of your handmaid: for Yahuah (LORD) will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fighteth the battles of Yahuah (LORD), and evil has not been found in you all your days.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:29: Yet a man is risen to pursue you, and to seek your soul: but the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God); and the souls of your enemies, them shall he sling out, as out of the middle of a sling.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:30: And it shall come to pass, when Yahuah (LORD) shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and shall have appointed you ruler over Yashar'el (Israel);
live.canon|1-samuel|25:31: That this shall be no grief unto you, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that you have shed blood causeless, or that my lord has avenged himself: but when Yahuah (LORD) shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember your handmaid.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:32: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which sent you this day to meet me:
live.canon|1-samuel|25:33: And blessed be your advice, and blessed be you, which have kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with my own hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:34: For in very deed, as Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) lives, which has kept me back from hurting you, except you had hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left unto Nabal by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:35: So David received of her hand that which she had brought him, and said unto her, Go up in peace to your house; see, I have hearkened to your voice, and have accepted your person.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:39: And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be Yahuah (LORD), that has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept his servant from evil: for Yahuah (LORD) has returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:40: And when the servants of David were come to Abigail to Carmel, they spake unto her, saying, David sent us unto you, to take you to him to wife.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:41: And she arose, and bowed herself on her face to the earth, and said, Behold, let your handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:1: And Samuel died; and all the Israelites were gathered together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:2: And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:3: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal did shear his sheep.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:5: And David sent out ten young men, and David said unto the young men, Get you up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:
live.canon|1-samuel|25:9: And when David’s young men came, they spake to Nabal according to all those words in the name of David, and ceased.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:10: And Nabal answered David’s servants, and said, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:11: Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give it unto men, whom I know not whence they be?
live.canon|1-samuel|25:12: So David’s young men turned their way, and went again, and came and told him all those sayings.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:14: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed on them.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:15: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:
live.canon|1-samuel|25:16: They were a wall unto us both by night and day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:18: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:19: And she said unto her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:20: And it was so, as she rode on the ass, that she came down by the covert of the hill, and, behold, David and his men came down against her; and she met them.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:22: So and more also do Elohim (God) unto the enemies of David, if I leave of all that pertain to him by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:23: And when Abigail saw David, she hasted, and lighted off the ass, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,
live.canon|1-samuel|25:36: And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken: wherefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:37: But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:38: And it came to pass about ten days after, that Yahuah (LORD) smote Nabal, that he died.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:42: And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon an ass, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:43: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they were also both of them his wives.
live.canon|1-samuel|25:44: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:24: And, behold, as your life was much set by this day in my eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of Yahuah (LORD), and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:1: And the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Does not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?
live.canon|1-samuel|26:6: Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with you.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:8: Then said Abishai to David, Elohim (God) has delivered your enemy into your hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray you, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:10: David said furthermore, As Yahuah (LORD) lives, Yahuah (LORD) shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:11: Yahuah (LORD) forbid that I should stretch forth my hand against the LORD’S anointed: but, I pray you, take you now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:14: And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answerest you not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who are you that cry to the king?
live.canon|1-samuel|26:15: And David said to Abner, Are not you a valiant man? and who is like to you in Yashar'el (Israel)? wherefore then have you not kept your lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king your lord.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:16: This thing is not good that you have done. As Yahuah (LORD) lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not kept your master, the LORD’S anointed. And now see where the king’s spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:17: And Saul knew David’s voice, and said, Is this your voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:18: And he said, Wherefore does my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in my hand?
live.canon|1-samuel|26:19: Now therefore, I pray you, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If Yahuah (LORD) have stirred you up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before Yahuah (LORD); for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of Yahuah (LORD), saying, Go, serve other gods.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:20: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of Yahuah (LORD): for the king of Yashar'el (Israel) is come out to seek a flea, as when one does hunt a partridge in the mountains.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:21: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do you harm, because my soul was precious in your eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:23: Yahuah (LORD) render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for Yahuah (LORD) delivered you into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth my hand against the LORD’S anointed.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:25: Then Saul said to David, Blessed be you, my son David: you shall both do great things, and also shall still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:2: Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Yashar'el (Israel) with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:3: And Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon, by the way. But David abode in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:4: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:5: And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:9: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD’S anointed, and be guiltless?
live.canon|1-samuel|26:12: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from Yahuah (LORD) was fallen upon them.
live.canon|1-samuel|26:13: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space being between them:
live.canon|1-samuel|26:22: And David answered and said, Behold the king’s spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:5: And David said unto Achish, If I have now found grace in your eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?
live.canon|1-samuel|27:8: And David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as you go to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:10: And Achish said, Whither have you made a road to day? And David said, Against the south of Yahudah (Judah), and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:11: And David saved neither man nor woman alive, to bring tidings to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us, saying, So did David, and so will be his manner all the while he dwells in the country of the Philistines.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:12: And Achish believed David, saying, He has made his people Yashar'el (Israel) utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:1: And David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Yashar'el (Israel): so shall I escape out of his hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:2: And David arose, and he passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:3: And David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, even David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s wife.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:4: And it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:6: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Yahudah (Judah) unto this day.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:7: And the time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.
live.canon|1-samuel|27:9: And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel, and returned, and came to Achish.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:1: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Yashar'el (Israel). And Achish said unto David, Know you assuredly, that you shall go out with me to battle, you and your men.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:2: And David said to Achish, Surely you shall know what your servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make you keeper of my head for ever.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:7: Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that has a familiar spirit at Endor.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:8: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray you, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto you.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:9: And the woman said unto him, Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest you a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
live.canon|1-samuel|28:10: And Saul sware to her by Yahuah (LORD), saying, As Yahuah (LORD) lives, there shall no punishment happen to you for this thing.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:12: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spake to Saul, saying, Why have you deceived me? for you are Saul.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:13: And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what saw you? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:14: And he said unto her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man comes up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:15: And Samuel said to Saul, Why have you disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and Elohim (God) is departed from me, and answers me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called you, that you may make known unto me what I shall do.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:16: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then do you ask of me, seeing Yahuah (LORD) is departed from you, and is become your enemy?
live.canon|1-samuel|28:17: And Yahuah (LORD) has done to him, as he spake by me: for Yahuah (LORD) has rent the kingdom out of your hand, and given it to your neighbour, even to David:
live.canon|1-samuel|28:18: Because you obeyedst not the voice of Yahuah (LORD), nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore has Yahuah (LORD) done this thing unto you this day.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:19: Moreover Yahuah (LORD) will also deliver Yashar'el (Israel) with you into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shall you and your sons be with me: Yahuah (LORD) also shall deliver the host of Yashar'el (Israel) into the hand of the Philistines.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:21: And the woman came unto Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, your handmaid has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto your words which you spoke unto me.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:22: Now therefore, I pray you, hearken you also unto the voice of your handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before you; and eat, that you may have strength, when you go on your way.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:3: Now Samuel was dead, and all Yashar'el (Israel) had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:4: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Yashar'el (Israel) together, and they pitched in Gilboa.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:5: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:6: And when Saul enquired of Yahuah (LORD), Yahuah (LORD) answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:20: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:23: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:24: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded it, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:
live.canon|1-samuel|28:25: And she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.
live.canon|1-samuel|28:11: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up unto you? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:3: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What do these Hebrews here? And Achish said unto the princes of the Philistines, Is not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Yashar'el (Israel), which has been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell unto me unto this day?
live.canon|1-samuel|29:4: And the princes of the Philistines were wroth with him; and the princes of the Philistines said unto him, Make this fellow return, that he may go again to his place which you have appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for wherewith should he reconcile himself unto his master? should it not be with the heads of these men?
live.canon|1-samuel|29:6: Then Achish called David, and said unto him, Surely, as Yahuah (LORD) lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the host is good in my sight: for I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming unto me unto this day: nevertheless the lords favour you not.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:7: Wherefore now return, and go in peace, that you displease not the lords of the Philistines.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:8: And David said unto Achish, But what have I done? and what have you found in your servant so long as I have been with you unto this day, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king?
live.canon|1-samuel|29:9: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that you are good in my sight, as an angel of Elohim (God): notwithstanding the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:10: Wherefore now rise up early in the morning with your master’s servants that are come with you: and as soon as you be up early in the morning, and have light, depart.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:1: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites pitched by a fountain which is in Jezreel.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:2: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rereward with Achish.
live.canon|1-samuel|29:5: Is not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
live.canon|1-samuel|29:11: So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:7: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, I pray you, bring me hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:8: And David enquired at Yahuah (LORD), saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for you shall surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:13: And David said unto him, To whom belongest you? and whence are you? And he said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days agone I fell sick.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:14: We made an invasion upon the south of the Cherethites, and upon the coast which belongs to Yahudah (Judah), and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:15: And David said to him, Can you bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear unto me by Elohim (God), that you will neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring you down to this company.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:23: Then said David, You shall not do so, my brethren, with that which Yahuah (LORD) has given us, who has preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:24: For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goes down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:1: And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;
live.canon|1-samuel|30:2: And had taken the women captives, that were therein: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away, and went on their way.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:3: So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:4: Then David and the people that were with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:5: And David’s two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:6: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God).
live.canon|1-samuel|30:9: So David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:11: And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;
live.canon|1-samuel|30:12: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any water, three days and three nights.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:16: And when he had brought him down, behold, they were spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Yahudah (Judah).
live.canon|1-samuel|30:17: And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, which rode upon camels, and fled.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:18: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:19: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any thing that they had taken to them: David recovered all.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:20: And David took all the flocks and the herds, which they drave before those other cattle, and said, This is David’s spoil.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:21: And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that were with him: and when David came near to the people, he saluted them.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:22: Then answered all the wicked men and men of Belial, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them ought of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away, and depart.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:25: And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Yashar'el (Israel) unto this day.
live.canon|1-samuel|30:26: And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Yahudah (Judah), even to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of Yahuah (LORD);
live.canon|1-samuel|30:27: To them which were in Beth-el, and to them which were in south Ramoth, and to them which were in Jattir,
live.canon|1-samuel|30:28: And to them which were in Aroer, and to them which were in Siphmoth, and to them which were in Eshtemoa,
live.canon|1-samuel|30:29: And to them which were in Rachal, and to them which were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to them which were in the cities of the Kenites,
live.canon|1-samuel|30:30: And to them which were in Hormah, and to them which were in Chor-ashan, and to them which were in Athach,
live.canon|1-samuel|30:31: And to them which were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:4: Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw your sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:1: Now the Philistines fought against Yashar'el (Israel): and the men of Yashar'el (Israel) fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:2: And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, Saul’s sons.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:3: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:5: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:6: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:7: And when the men of Yashar'el (Israel) that were on the other side of the valley, and they that were on the other side Jordan, saw that the men of Yashar'el (Israel) fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:8: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:9: And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols, and among the people.
live.canon|1-samuel|31:10: And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

live.canon|1-thessalonians|1:2: We give thanks to Elohim (God) always for you all, making mention of you in our prayers;

live.canon|acts|16:27: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.

live.canon|acts|20:6: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
live.canon|acts|20:7: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
live.canon|acts|20:8: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
live.canon|acts|20:9: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
live.canon|acts|20:10: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
live.canon|acts|20:11: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
live.canon|acts|20:12: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
live.canon|acts|20:13: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
live.canon|acts|20:14: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
live.canon|acts|20:15: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
live.canon|acts|20:16: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
live.canon|acts|20:17: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
live.canon|acts|20:20: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
live.canon|acts|20:22: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
live.canon|acts|20:23: Save that the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
live.canon|acts|20:26: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
live.canon|acts|20:27: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of Elohim (God).
live.canon|acts|20:29: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
live.canon|acts|20:30: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
live.canon|acts|20:31: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
live.canon|acts|20:32: And now, brethren, I commend you to Elohim (God), and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
live.canon|acts|20:33: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
live.canon|acts|20:36: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
live.canon|acts|20:37: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
live.canon|acts|20:38: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
live.canon|acts|20:34: Yea, you yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
live.canon|acts|20:18: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, You know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
live.canon|acts|20:25: And now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of Elohim (God), shall see my face no more.
live.canon|acts|20:28: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) has made you overseers, to feed the church of Elohim (God), which he has purchased with his own blood.
live.canon|acts|20:19: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Yahudim (Jews):
live.canon|acts|20:21: Testifying both to the Yahudim (Jews), and also to the Greeks, repentance toward Elohim (God), and faith toward our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).
live.canon|acts|20:24: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of Lord Yahusha (Jesus), to testify the gospel of the grace of Elohim (God).
live.canon|acts|20:35: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring you ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of Lord Yahusha (Jesus), how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
live.canon|acts|21:1: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
live.canon|acts|21:2: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
live.canon|acts|21:3: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
live.canon|acts|21:4: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
live.canon|acts|21:5: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
live.canon|acts|21:6: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
live.canon|acts|21:7: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
live.canon|acts|21:8: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
live.canon|acts|21:9: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
live.canon|acts|21:10: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.
live.canon|acts|21:12: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
live.canon|acts|21:15: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
live.canon|acts|21:16: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cæsarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
live.canon|acts|21:17: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
live.canon|acts|21:18: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
live.canon|acts|21:19: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things Elohim (God) had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
live.canon|acts|21:25: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
live.canon|acts|21:26: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
live.canon|acts|21:27: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Yahudim (Jews) which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
live.canon|acts|21:29: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
live.canon|acts|21:30: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
live.canon|acts|21:31: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
live.canon|acts|21:32: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
live.canon|acts|21:33: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
live.canon|acts|21:34: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
live.canon|acts|21:35: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
live.canon|acts|21:36: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
live.canon|acts|21:40: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
live.canon|acts|21:38: Are not you that Egyptian, which before these days made an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
live.canon|acts|21:39: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Yahudi (Jew) of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech you, suffer me to speak unto the people.
live.canon|acts|21:11: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus says the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), So shall the Yahudim (Jews) at Jerusalem bind the man that owns this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
live.canon|acts|21:21: And they are informed of you, that you teach all the Yahudim (Jews) which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
live.canon|acts|21:22: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that you are come.
live.canon|acts|21:23: Do therefore this that we say to you: We have four men which have a vow on them;
live.canon|acts|21:24: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning you, are nothing; but that you thyself also walk orderly, and keepest the law.
live.canon|acts|21:28: Crying out, Men of Yashar'el (Israel), help: This is the man, that teaches all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and has polluted this holy place.
live.canon|acts|21:37: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto you? Who said, Can you speak Greek?
live.canon|acts|21:14: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
live.canon|acts|21:13: Then Paul answered, What mean you to weep and to break my heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of Lord Yahusha (Jesus).
live.canon|acts|21:20: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, You see, brother, how many thousands of Yahudim (Jews) there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
live.canon|acts|22:4: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
live.canon|acts|22:6: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
live.canon|acts|22:1: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear you my defence which I make now unto you.
live.canon|acts|22:9: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
live.canon|acts|22:11: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
live.canon|acts|22:12: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Yahudim (Jews) which dwelt there,
live.canon|acts|22:17: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
live.canon|acts|22:22: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
live.canon|acts|22:23: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
live.canon|acts|22:24: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
live.canon|acts|22:25: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
live.canon|acts|22:28: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
live.canon|acts|22:29: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
live.canon|acts|22:30: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Yahudim (Jews), he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
live.canon|acts|22:7: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me?
live.canon|acts|22:2: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he says,)
live.canon|acts|22:3: I am verily a man which am a Yahudi (Jew), born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward Elohim (God), as you all are this day.
live.canon|acts|22:5: As also the high priest does bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
live.canon|acts|22:8: And I answered, Who are you, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Yahusha (Jesus) of Nazareth, whom you persecute.
live.canon|acts|22:13: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive your sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
live.canon|acts|22:14: And he said, The Elohim (God) of our fathers has chosen you, that you should know his will, and see that Just One, and should hear the voice of his mouth.
live.canon|acts|22:15: For you shall be his witness unto all men of what you have seen and heard.
live.canon|acts|22:18: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get you quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive your testimony concerning me.
live.canon|acts|22:20: And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
live.canon|acts|22:21: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send you far hence unto the Gentiles.
live.canon|acts|22:26: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what you do: for this man is a Roman.
live.canon|acts|22:27: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yea.
live.canon|acts|22:10: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told you of all things which are appointed for you to do.
live.canon|acts|22:16: And now why tarriest you? arise, and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
live.canon|acts|22:19: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on you:
live.canon|acts|23:1: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before Elohim (God) until this day.
live.canon|acts|23:2: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
live.canon|acts|23:6: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
live.canon|acts|23:7: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
live.canon|acts|23:8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
