live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:26: And now let it not weary thee, and turn not to the right hand nor the left, but fly and go by a direct way, that thou mayst preserve the command of the Mighty One, according as I said unto thee.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:1: These are the words of that epistle which Baruch the son of Neriah sent to the nine and a half tribes, which were across the river Euphrates, in which these things were written.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:2: Thus saith Baruch the son of Neriah to the brethren carried into captivity: 'Mercy and peace. I bear in mind, my brethren, the love of Him who created us, who loved us from of old, and never hated us, but above all educated us.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:3: And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:4: Wherefore I have been the more careful to leave you the words of this epistle before I die, that ye may be comforted regarding the evils which have come upon you, and that ye may be grieved also regarding the evil that has befallen your brethren; and again, also, that ye may justify His judgement which He has decreed against you that ye should be carried away captive—for what ye have suffered is disproportioned to what ye have done—in order
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:5: that, at the last times, ye may be found worthy of your fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:6: Therefore, if ye consider that ye have now suffered those things for your good, that ye may not finally be condemned and tormented, then ye will receive eternal hope; if above all ye destroy from your heart vain error, on account of which ye departed hence.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:7: For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|79:1: Now, my brethren, learn first what befell Zion: how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against us.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|79:2: For we have sinned against Him who made us, and we have not kept the commandments which he commanded us, yet he hath not chastened us as we deserved.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|79:3: For what befell you we also suffer in a pre-eminent degree, for it befell us also.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:1: And now, my brethren, I make known unto you that when the enemy had surrounded the city, the angels of the El Elyon (Most High) were sent, and they overthrew the fortifications of the strong wall, and they destroyed the firm iron corners, which could not be rooted out.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:2: Nevertheless, they hid all the vessels of the sanctuary, lest the enemy should get possession of them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:3: And when they had done these things, they delivered thereupon to the enemy the overthrown wall, and the plundered house, and the burnt temple, and the people who were overcome because they were delivered up, lest the enemy should boast and say: 'Thus by force have we been able to lay waste even the house of the El Elyon (Most High) in war.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:4: Your brethren also have they bound and led away to Babylon, and have caused them to dwell there.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:5: But we have been left here, being very few.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:6: This is the tribulation about which I wrote to you.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:7: For assuredly I know that (the consolation of) the inhabitants of Zion consoleth you: so far as ye knew that it was prospered (your consolation) was greater than the tribulation which ye endured in having to depart from it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:1: But regarding consolation, hear ye the word.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:2: For I was mourning regarding Zion, and I prayed for mercy from the El Elyon (Most High), and I said:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:3: 'How long will these things endure for us? And will these evils come upon us always?'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:4: And the Mighty One did according to the multitude of His mercies, And the El Elyon (Most High) according to the greatness of His compassion, And He revealed unto me the word, that I might receive consolation, And He showed me visions that I should not again endure anguish, And He made known to me the mystery of the times, And the advent of the hours he showed me.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:1: Therefore, my brethren, I have written to you, that ye may comfort yourselves regarding the multitude of your tribulations.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:2: For know ye that our Maker will assuredly avenge us on all our enemies, according to all that they have done to us, also that the consummation which the El Elyon (Most High) will make is very nigh, and His mercy that is coming, and the consummation of His judgement, is by no means far off.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:3: For lo! we see now the multitude of the prosperity of the Gentiles, Though they act impiously, But they shall be like a vapour:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:4: And we behold the multitude of their power, Though they do wickedly, But they shall be made like unto a drop:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:5: And we see the firmness of their might, Though they resist the Mighty One every hour, But they shall be accounted as spittle.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:6: And we consider the glory of their greatness, Though they do not keep the statutes of the El Elyon (Most High), But as smoke shall they pass away.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:7: And we meditate on the beauty of their gracefulness, Though they have to do with pollutions, But as grass that withers shall they fade away.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:8: And we consider the strength of their cruelty, Though they remember not the end (thereof), But as a wave that passes shall they be broken.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:9: And we remark the boastfulness of their might, Though they deny the beneficence of Elohim (God), who gave (it) to them, But they shall pass away as a passing cloud.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:1: [For the El Elyon (Most High) will assuredly hasten His times, And He will assuredly bring on His hours.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:2: And He will assuredly judge those who are in His world, And will visit in truth all things by means of all their hidden works.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:3: And He will assuredly examine the secret thoughts, And that which is laid up in the secret chambers of all the members of man, And will make (them) manifest in the presence of all with reproof.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:4: Let none therefore of these present things ascend into your hearts, but above all let us be expectant, because that which is promised to us shall come.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:5: And let us not now look unto the delights of the Gentiles in the present, but let us remember what has been promised to us in the end.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:6: For the ends of the times and of the seasons and whatsoever is with them shall assuredly pass by together.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:7: The consummation, moreover, of the age shall then show the great might of its ruler, when all things come to judgement.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:8: Do ye therefore prepare your hearts for that which before ye believed, lest ye come to be in bondage in both worlds, so that ye be led away captive here and be tormented there.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:9: For that which exists now or which has passed away, or which is to come, in all these things, neither is the evil fully evil, nor again the good fully good.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:10: For all healthinesses of this time are turning into diseases,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:11: And all might of this time is turning into weakness, And all the force of this time is turning into impotence,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:12: And every energy of youth is turning into old age and consummation, And every beauty of gracefulness of this time is turning faded and hateful,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:13: And every proud dominion of the present is turning into humiliation and shame,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:14: And every praise of the glory of this time is turning into the shame of silence, And every vain splendour and insolence of this time is turning into voiceless ruin.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:15: And every delight and joy of this time is turning to worms and corruption,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:16: And every clamour of the pride of this time is turning into dust and stillness.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:17: And every possession of riches of this time is being turned into Sheol alone,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:18: And all the rapine of passion of this time is turning into involuntary death, And every passion of the lusts of this time is turning into a judgement of torment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:19: And every artifice and craftiness of this time is turning into a proof of the truth,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:20: And every sweetness of unguents of this time is turning into judgement and condemnation,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:21: And every love of lying is turning to contumely through truth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:22: Since therefore all these things are done now, does anyone think that they will not be avenged? But the consummation of all things will come to the truth.]
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:1: Behold! I have therefore made known unto you (these things) whilst I live; for I have said (it) that ye should learn the things that are excellent; for the Mighty One hath commanded me to instruct you: and I will set before you some of the commandments of His judgement before I die.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:2: Remember that formerly Moses assuredly called heaven and earth to witness against you and said: 'If ye transgress the law ye shall be dispersed, but if ye keep it ye shall be kept.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:3: And other things also he used to say unto you when ye the twelve tribes were together in the desert.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:4: And after his death ye cast them away from you: on this account there came upon you what had been predicted.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:5: And now Moses used to tell you before they befell you, and lo! they have befallen you: for ye have forsaken the law.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:6: Lo! I also say unto you after ye have suffered, that if ye obey those things which have been said unto you, ye will receive from the Mighty One whatever has been laid up and reserved for you.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:7: Moreover, let this epistle be for a testimony between me and you, that ye may remember the commandments of the Mighty One, and that also there may be to me a defence in the presence of Him who sent me.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:8: And remember ye the law and Zion, and the holy land and your brethren, and the covenant of your fathers, and forget not the festivals and the sabbaths.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:9: And deliver ye this epistle and the traditions of the law to your sons after you, as also your fathers delivered (them) to you.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:10: And at all times make request perseveringly and pray diligently with your whole heart that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you, and that He may not reckon the multitude of your sins, but remember the rectitude of your fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|84:11: For if He judge us not according to the multitude of His mercies, woe unto all us who are born.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:1: Know ye, moreover, that in former times and in the generations of old our fathers had helpers, Righteous men and holy prophets:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:2: Nay more, we were in our own land, [And they helped us when we sinned], And they interceded for us with Him who made us, Because they trusted in their works], And the Mighty One heard their prayer and forgave us.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:3: But now the righteous have been gathered, And the prophets have fallen asleep, And we also have gone forth from the land, And Zion has been taken from us, And we have nothing now save the Mighty One and His law.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:4: If therefore we direct and dispose our hearts, We shall receive everything that we lost, And much better things than we lost by many times.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:5: For what we have lost was subject to corruption, And what we shall receive shall not be corruptible.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:6: [Moreover, also, I have written thus to our brethren to Babylon, that to them also I may attest these very things.]
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:7: And let all those things aforesaid be always before your eyes, Because we are still in the spirit and the power of our liberty.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:8: Again, moreover, the El Elyon (Most High) also is long-suffering towards us here, And He hath shown to us that which is to be, And hath not concealed from us what will befall in the end.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:9: Before therefore judgement exact its own, And truth that which is its due, Let us prepare our soul That we may possess, and not be taken possession of, And that we may hope and not be put to shame, And that we may rest with our fathers, and not be tormented with our enemies.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:10: For the youth of the world is past, And the strength of the creation already exhausted, And the advent of the times is very short, Yea, they have passed by; And the pitcher is near to the cistern, And the ship to the port, And the course of the journey to the city, And life to (its) consummation.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:11: And again prepare your souls, so that when ye sail and ascend from the ship ye may have rest and not be condemned when ye depart.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:12: For lo! when the El Elyon (Most High) will bring to pass all these things, There shall not there be again [a place of repentance, nor] a limit to the times, Nor a duration for the hours, Nor a change of ways, Nor place for prayer, Nor sending of petitions, Nor receiving of knowledge, Nor giving of love, Nor place of repentance for the soul, Nor supplication for offences, Nor intercession of the fathers, Nor prayer of the prophets, Nor help of the righteous.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:13: There there is the sentence of corruption, The way of fire, And the path which bringeth to Gehenna.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:14: On this account there is one law by one, One age and an end for all who are in it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|85:15: Then He will preserve those whom He can forgive, And at the same time destroy those who are polluted with sins.]
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|86:1: When therefore ye receive this my epistle, read it in your congregations with care.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|86:2: And meditate thereon, above all on the days of your fasts.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|86:3: And bear me in mind by means of this epistle, as I also bear you in mind in it, and always. Fare ye well.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|87:1: And it came to pass when I had ended all the words of this epistle, and had written it sedulously to its close, that I folded it, and sealed it carefully, and bound it to the neck of the eagle, and dismissed and sent it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|50:1: And He answered and said unto me: 'Hear, Baruch, this word, And write in the remembrance of thy heart all that thou shalt learn.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|50:2: For the earth shall then assuredly restore the dead, [Which it now receives, in order to preserve them]. It shall make no change in their form, But as it has received, so shall it restore them, And as I delivered them unto it, so also shall it raise them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|50:3: For then it will be necessary to show to the living that the dead have come to life again, and that those who had departed have returned (again).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|50:4: And it shall come to pass, when they have severally recognized those whom they now know, then judgement shall grow strong, and those things which before were spoken of shall come.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:1: Observe, therefore, my children, the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), And keep His law; Depart from wrath, And hate lying, That Yahuah (Lord) may dwell among you, And Beliar may flee from you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:2: Speak truth each one with his neighbour, So shall ye not fall into wrath and confusion; But ye shall be in peace, having the Elohim (God) of peace, So shall no war prevail over you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:3: Love Yahuah (Lord) through all your life, And one another with a true heart.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:4: I know that in the last days ye shall depart from Yahuah (Lord), And ye shall provoke Levi unto anger, And fight against Yahudah (Judah); But ye shall not prevail against them, For an angel of Yahuah (Lord) shall guide them both; For by them shall Yashar'el (Israel) stand.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:5: And whensoever ye depart from Yahuah (Lord), ye shall walk in all evil and work the abominations of the Gentiles, going a-whoring after women of the lawless ones, while with all wickedness the spirits of wickedness work 'in you',
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:6: [For I have read in the book of Enoch, the righteous, that your prince is Satan, and that all the spirits of wickedness and pride will conspire to attend constantly on the sons of Levi, to cause them to sin before Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:7: And my sons will draw near to Levi, And sin with them in all things; And the sons of Yahudah (Judah) will be covetous, Plundering other men's goods like lions.]
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:8: Therefore shall ye be led away [with them] into captivity, And there shall ye receive all the plagues of Egypt, And all the evils of the Gentiles.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:9: And so when ye return to Yahuah (Lord) ye shall obtain mercy, And He shall bring you into His sanctuary, And He shall give you peace.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:10: And there shall arise unto you from the tribe of [Yahudah (Judah) and of] Levi the salvation of Yahuah (Lord); And he shall make war against Beliar, And execute an everlasting vengeance on our enemies;
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:11: And the captivity shall he take from Beliar [the souls of the saints], And turn disobedient hearts unto Yahuah (Lord), And give to them that call upon him eternal peace.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:12: And the saints shall rest in Eden, And in the New Jerusalem will the righteous rejoice, And it shall be unto the glory of Elohim (God) for ever.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|83:13: And no longer shall Jerusalem endure desolation, Nor Yashar'el (Israel) be led captive; For Yahuah (Lord) shall be in the midst of it [living amongst men], And the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel) shall reign over it [in humility and in poverty; and he who believeth on Him shall reign amongst men in truth].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:1: And now, fear Yahuah (Lord), my children, and beware of Satan and his spirits.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:2: Draw near unto Elohim (God) and to the angel that intercedeth for you, for he is a mediator between Elohim (God) and man, and for the peace of Yashar'el (Israel) he shall stand up against the kingdom of the enemy.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:3: Therefore is the enemy eager to destroy all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:4: For he knoweth that on the day on which Yashar'el (Israel) shall repent, the kingdom of the enemy shall be brought to an end.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:5: For the very angel of peace shall strengthen Yashar'el (Israel), that it fall not into the extremity of evil.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:6: And it shall be in the time of the lawlessness of Yashar'el (Israel), that Yahuah (Lord) will (not) depart from them, but will transform them into a nation that doeth His will, for none of the angels will be equal unto him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:7: And His name shall be in every place of Yashar'el (Israel), 'and among the Gentiles'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:8: Keep, therefore, yourselves, my children, from every evil work, And cast away wrath and all lying, And love truth and long-suffering.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:9: And the things which ye have heard from your father, do ye also impart to your children [that the Saviour of the Gentiles may receive you; for he is true and long-suffering, meek and lowly, and teacheth by his works the law of Elohim (God)].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:10: Depart, therefore, from all unrighteousness, and cleave unto the righteousness of Elohim (God), and your race will be saved for ever.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|84:11: And bury me near my fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|85:1: And when he had said these things he kissed them, and fell asleep at a good old age.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|85:2: And his sons buried him. And after that they carried up 'his bones', and placed them near Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|85:3: [Nevertheless, 'Dan' prophesied unto them that they should forget their Elohim (God), and should be alienated from the land of their inheritance 'and from the race of Israel', and from the family of 'their seed'.]
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:1: The copy of the testament of Naphtali, which he ordained at the time of his death in the hundred and thirtieth year of his life.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:2: When his sons were gathered together in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, while still in good health, he made then a feast of food and wine.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:3: And after he was awake in the morning, he said to them, I am dying; and they believed him not.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:4: And as he glorified Yahuah (Lord), he grew strong and said that after yesterday's feast he should die. Hear, my children, ye sons of Naphtali, hear the words of your father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:5: And he began then to say:
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:6: I was born from Bilhah; 'and' because Rachel dealt craftily, and gave Bilhah in place of herself to Jacob, and she conceived and bare me upon Rachel's knees, 'therefore' she called my name Naphtali.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:7: For Rachel loved me very much because I was born upon her knees; and when I was still young she was wont to kiss me, and say: May I have a brother of thine from mine own womb, like unto thee.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:8: Whence also Joseph was like unto me 'in all things', according to the prayers of Rachel.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:9: Now my mother was Bilhah, daughter of Rotheus the brother of Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, who was born on one and the self-same day with Rachel.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:10: And Rotheus was of the family of Abraham, a Chaldean, Elohim (God)-fearing, free-born, and noble.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:11: And he was taken captive and was bought by Laban; and he gave him Euna his handmaid to wife, and she bore a daughter, and called her name Zilpah, after the name of the village in which he had been taken captive.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|86:12: And next she bore Bilhah, saying: My daughter hastens after what is new, for immediately that she was born she seized the breast and hastened to suck it.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:10: For if thou bid the eye to hear, it cannot; so neither while ye are in darkness can ye do the works of light.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:1: And I was swift on my feet like the deer, and my father Jacob appointed me for all messages, and as a deer did he give me his blessing.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:2: For as the potter knoweth the vessel, how much it is to contain, and bringeth clay accordingly, so also doth Yahuah (Lord) make the body after the likeness of the spirit, and according to the capacity of the body doth He implant the spirit.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:3: And the one does not fall short of the other by a third part of a hair; for by weight, and measure, and rule was all the creation made.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:4: And as the potter knoweth the use of each vessel, what it is meet for, so also doth Yahuah (Lord) know the body, how far it will persist in goodness, and when it beginneth in evil.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:5: For there is no inclination or thought which Yahuah (Lord) knoweth not, for He created every man after His own image.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:6: For as a man's strength, so also is his work; as his mind, so also is his skill; and as his purpose, so also is his achievement; and as his heart, so also is his mouth; as his eye, so also is his sleep; as his soul, so also is his word, either in the law of Yahuah (Lord) or in the works of Beliar.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:7: And as there is a division between light and darkness, between seeing and hearing, so also is there a division between man and man, and between woman and woman; and it is not to be said that the one is like the other either in face or in mind.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:8: 'For' Elohim (God) made all things good in their order, the five senses in the head, and He joined on the neck to the head, adding to it the hair also for comeliness and glory, then the heart for understanding, the belly for excrement, and the stomach for grinding, the windpipe for taking in (the breath), the liver for wrath, the gall for bitterness, the spleen for laughter, the reins 'for prudence, the muscles of the loins' for power, the lungs for drawing in, the loins for strength, and so forth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|87:9: So 'then', my children, let all your works be done in order with good intent in the fear of Elohim (God), and do nothing disorderly in scorn or out of its due season.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|88:1: Be ye, therefore, not eager to corrupt your doings through covetousness or with vain words to beguile your souls; because if ye keep silence in purity of heart, ye shall understand how to hold fast the will of Elohim (God), and to cast away the will of Beliar.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|88:2: Sun and moon and stars change not their order; so do ye also change not the law of Elohim (God) in the disorderliness of your doings.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|88:3: The Gentiles went astray, and forsook Yahuah (Lord), and changed their order, and obeyed stocks and stones, spirits of deceit.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|88:4: But ye shall not be so, my children, recognising in the firmament, in the earth, and in the sea, and in all created things, Yahuah (Lord) who made all things, that ye become not as Sodom, which changed the order of nature.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|88:5: In like manner the Watchers also changed the order of their nature, whom Yahuah (Lord) cursed at the flood, on whose account He made the earth without inhabitant and fruitless.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|89:1: These things I say unto you, my children, for I have read in the writing of Enoch that ye yourselves also shall depart from Yahuah (Lord), walking according to all the lawlessness of the Gentiles, and ye shall do according to all the wickedness of Sodom.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|89:2: And Yahuah (Lord) shall bring captivity upon you, and 'there' shall ye serve your enemies, and ye shall be bowed down with every affliction and tribulation, until Yahuah (Lord) have consumed you all.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|89:3: And after ye have become minished and made few, ye shall return and acknowledge Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God); and He shall bring you back into your own land, according to His abundant mercy.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|89:4: And it shall be, that after that they come into the land of their fathers, they shall again forget Yahuah (Lord) and become ungodly.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|89:5: And Yahuah (Lord) shall scatter them upon the face of all the earth, until the compassion of Yahuah (Lord) shall come, a man working righteousness and working mercy unto all them that are afar off, and to them that are near.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:1: For in the fortieth year of my life, I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, on the east of Jerusalem, that the sun and the moon were standing still.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:2: And behold Isaac, the father of my father, said to us: Run and lay hold of them, each one according to his strength; 'and to him that seizeth them will the sun and moon belong'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:3: And we all of us ran together, and Levi laid hold of the sun, and Yahudah (Judah) outstripped the others and seized the moon, and they were both of them lifted up with them.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:4: And when Levi became as a sun, 'lo', a certain young man gave to him twelve branches of palm; and Yahudah (Judah) was bright as the moon, and under their feet were twelve rays.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:5: [And the two, Levi and Yahudah (Judah), ran, and laid hold of them.]
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:6: And lo, a bull upon the earth, with two great horns, and an eagle's wings upon his back; and we wished to seize him, but could not.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:7: But Joseph came, and seized him, and ascended up with him on high.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|90:8: And I saw, for I was there, and behold a holy writing appeared to us, saying: Assyrians, Medes, Persians, [Chaldeans,] Syrians, shall possess in captivity the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:1: And again, after seven days, I saw our father Jacob standing by the sea of Jamnia, and we were with him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:2: And, behold, there came a ship sailing by, without sailors or pilot; and there was written upon the ship, The ship of Jacob.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:3: And our father saith to us: Come let us embark on our ship.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:4: And when we had gone on board, there arose a vehement storm, and a mighty tempest of wind; and our father, who was holding the helm, departed from us.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:5: And we, being tost with the tempest, were borne along over the sea; and the ship was filled with water, (and was) pounded by mighty waves, until it was broken up.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:6: And Joseph fled away upon a little boat, 'and we all were divided upon nine planks,' and Levi and Yahudah (Judah) were together.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:7: And we were all scattered unto the ends of the earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:8: Then Levi, girt about with sackcloth, prayed for us all unto Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|91:9: And when the storm ceased, the ship reached the land, 'as it were' in peace. And, lo, our father came, and we all rejoiced with one accord.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|92:1: These two dreams I told to my father; and he said to me: These things must be fulfilled in their season, after that Yashar'el (Israel) hath endured many things.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|92:2: Then my father saith unto me: I believe Elohim (God) that Joseph liveth, for I see 'always' that Yahuah (Lord) numbereth him with you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|92:3: And he said, weeping: Ah me, my son, Joseph, thou livest, though I behold thee not, and thou seest not Jacob that begat thee.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|92:4: He caused me also, therefore, to weep by these words, and I burned in my heart to declare that 'Joseph' had been sold, but I feared my brethren.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:1: And lo! my children, I have shown unto you the last times, how everything shall come to pass in Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:2: Do ye also, 'therefore,' charge your children that they be united to Levi and to Yahudah (Judah); For through them shall salvation arise unto Yashar'el (Israel), And in them shall Jacob be blessed.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:3: For through their tribes shall Elohim (God) appear [dwelling among men] on earth, To save the race of Yashar'el (Israel), And to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:4: If ye work that which is good, my children, 'Both' men and angels shall bless you; And Elohim (God) shall be glorified among the Gentiles through you, And the devil shall flee from you, 'And the wild beasts shall fear you,' And Yahuah (Lord) shall love you, [And the angels shall cleave to you].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:5: As a man who has trained a child well is kept in kindly remembrance; So also for a good work there is a good remembrance before Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:6: But him who doeth not that which is good, 'Both' angels and men shall curse, And Elohim (God) shall be dishonoured among the Gentiles through him, And the devil shall make him as his own peculiar instrument, And every wild beast shall master him, And Yahuah (Lord) shall hate him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:7: For the commandments of the law are twofold, 'And' through prudence must they be fulfilled.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:8: For there is a season for a man to embrace his wife, And a season to abstain therefrom for his prayer.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:9: So, then, there are two commandments; and, unless they be done in due order, they bring 'very great' sin 'upon men'. So also is it with the other commandments.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|93:10: Be ye therefore wise in Elohim (God), 'my children,' and prudent, understanding the order of His commandments, and the laws of every word, that Yahuah (Lord) may love you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|94:1: And when he had charged them with many such words, he exhorted them that they should remove his bones to Hebron, and that they should bury him with his fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|94:2: And when he had eaten and drunken with a merry heart, he covered his face and died.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|94:3: And his sons did according to all that Naphtali their father had commanded them.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:1: The copy of the testament of Gad, what things he spake unto his sons, in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life, saying unto them:
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:2: 'Hearken, my children,' I was the ninth son born to Jacob, and I was valiant in keeping the flocks.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:3: Accordingly I guarded 'at night' the flock; and whenever the lion came, 'or the wolf,' or any wild beast against the fold, I pursued it, and 'overtaking (it)' I seized its foot with my hand and hurled it about a stone's throw, and so killed it.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:4: Now Joseph my brother was feeding the flock with us for upwards of thirty days, and being young, he fell sick by reason of the heat.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:5: And he returned to Hebron to our father, who made him lie down near him, because he loved him greatly.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:6: And Joseph told our father that the sons of 'Zilpah and' Bilhah were slaying the best 'of the flock' and eating them against the judgment of Reuben and Yahudah (Judah).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:7: For he saw that I had delivered a lamb out of the mouth of the bear, and put the bear to death; but had slain the lamb, being grieved concerning it that it could not live, and that we had eaten it.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:8: And regarding this matter I was wroth with Joseph 'until the day that he was sold.'
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|95:9: And the spirit of hatred was in me, and I wished not either to hear of Joseph with the ears, or to see him with the eyes, because he rebuked us to our faces 'saying' that we were eating of the flock without Yahudah (Judah). For whatsoever things he told our father, he believed him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|96:1: I confess now my sin, my children, that oftentimes I wished to kill him, because I hated him from my heart.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|96:2: Moreover, I hated him yet more for his dreams; and I wished to lick him out of the land of the living, even as an ox licketh up the grass of the field.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|96:3: And Yahudah (Judah) sold him secretly to the Ishmaelites.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|96:4: And thus through covetousness we were bent on slaying him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|96:5: Thus the Elohim (God) of our fathers delivered him from our hands, that we should not work great lawlessness in Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|97:1: And now, my children, hearken to the words of truth to work righteousness, and all the law of the El Elyon (Most High), and go not astray through the spirit of hatred, for it is evil in all the doings of men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|97:2: Whatsoever a man doeth the hater abominates him: and though a man worketh the law of Yahuah (Lord), he praiseth him not; though a man feareth Yahuah (Lord), and taketh pleasure in that which is righteous, he loveth him not.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|97:3: He dispraiseth the truth, he envieth him that prospers, he welcometh evil-speaking, he loveth arrogance, for hatred blindeth his soul; as I 'also then' looked on Joseph.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:1: The copy of the Testament of Reuben, even the commands which he gave his sons before he died in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:2: Two years after the death of Joseph his brother, when Reuben fell ill, his sons and his sons' sons were gathered together to visit him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:3: And he said to them: My children, behold I am dying, and go the way of my fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:4: And seeing there Yahudah (Judah), and Gad, and Asher, his brethren, he said to them: Raise me up, that I may tell to my brethren and to my children what things I have hidden in my heart, for behold now at length I am passing away.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:5: And he arose and kissed them, and said unto them: Hear, my brethren, and do ye, my children, give ear to Reuben your father, in the commands which I give you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:6: And behold I call to witness against you this day the Elohim (God) of heaven, that ye walk not in the ignorance of youth and fornication, wherein I was poured out, and defiled the bed of my father Jacob.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:7: And I tell you that He smote me with a sore plague in my loins for seven months; and had not my father Jacob prayed for me to Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord) would have destroyed me.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:8: For I was thirty years old when I wrought the evil thing before Yahuah (Lord), and for seven months I was sick unto death.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:9: And after this I repented with set purpose of my soul for seven years before Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|1:10: And wine and strong drink I drank not, and flesh entered not into my mouth, and I eat no pleasant food; but I mourned over my sin, for it was great, such as had not been in Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:1: And now hear me, my children, what things I saw concerning the seven spirits of deceit, when I repented.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:2: Seven spirits therefore are appointed against man, and they are the leaders in the works of youth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:3: [And seven other spirits are given to him at his creation, that through them should be done every work of man,
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:4: The first is the spirit of life, with which the constitution (of man) is created. The second is the sense of sight, with which ariseth desire.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:5: The third is the sense of hearing, with which cometh teaching. The fourth is the sense of smell, with which tastes are given to draw air and breath.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:6: The fifth is the power of speech, with which cometh knowledge.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:7: The sixth is the sense of taste, with which cometh the eating of meats and drinks; and by it strength is produced, for in food is the foundation of strength.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:8: The seventh is the power of procreation and sexual intercourse, with which through love of pleasure sins enter in.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|2:9: Wherefore it is the last in order of creation, and the first in that of youth, because it is filled with ignorance, and leadeth the youth as a blind man to a pit, and as a beast to a precipice.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:1: Besides all these there is an eighth spirit of sleep, with which is brought about the trance of nature and the image of death.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:2: With these spirits are mingled the spirits of error.]
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:3: First, the spirit of fornication is seated in the nature and in the senses; the second, the spirit of insatiableness, in the belly;
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:4: The third, the spirit of fighting, in the liver and gall. The fourth is the spirit of obsequiousness and chicanery, that through officious attention one may be fair in seeming.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:5: The fifth is the spirit of pride, that one may be boastful and arrogant. The sixth is the spirit of lying, in perdition and in jealousy, to practise deceits, and concealments from kindred and friends.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:6: The seventh is the spirit of injustice, with which are thefts and acts of rapacity, that a man may fulfil the desire of his heart; for injustice worketh together with the other spirits by the taking of gifts.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:7: [And with all these the spirit of sleep is joined which is (that) of error and fantasy.]
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:8: And so perisheth every young man, darkening his mind from the truth, and not understanding the law of Elohim (God), nor obeying the admonitions of his fathers, as befell me also in my youth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:9: And now, my children, love the truth, and it will preserve you: hear ye the words of Reuben your father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:10: Pay no heed to the face of a woman, Nor associate with another man's wife, Nor meddle with affairs of womankind.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:11: For had I not seen Bilhah bathing in a covered place, I had not fallen into this great iniquity.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:12: For my mind taking in the thought of the woman's nakedness, suffered me not to sleep until I had wrought the abominable thing.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:13: For while Jacob our father had gone to Isaac his father, when we were in Eder, near to Ephrath in Bethlehem, Bilhah became drunk and was asleep uncovered in her chamber.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:14: Having therefore gone in and beheld her nakedness, I wrought the impiety without her perceiving it, and leaving her sleeping I departed.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|3:15: And forthwith an angel of Elohim (God) revealed to my father concerning my impiety, and he came and mourned over me, and touched her no more.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:1: Pay no heed, therefore, my children, to the beauty of women, nor set your mind on their affairs; but walk in singleness of heart in the fear of Yahuah (Lord), and expend labour on good works, and on study and on your flocks, until Yahuah (Lord) give you a wife, whom He will, that ye suffer not as I did.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:2: For until my father's death I had not boldness to look in his face, or to speak to any of my brethren, because of the reproach.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:3: Even until now my conscience causeth me anguish on account of my impiety.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:4: And yet my father comforted me much, and prayed for me unto Yahuah (Lord), that the anger of Yahuah (Lord) might pass from me, even as Yahuah (Lord) showed. And thenceforth until now I have been on my guard and sinned not.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:5: Therefore, my children, I say unto you, observe all things whatsoever I command you, and ye shall not sin.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:6: For a pit unto the soul is the sin of fornication, separating it from Elohim (God), and bringing it near to idols, because it deceiveth the mind and understanding, and leadeth down young men into Hades before their time.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:7: For many hath fornication destroyed; because, though a man be old or noble, or rich or poor, he bringeth reproach upon himself with the sons of men and derision with Beliar.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:8: For hear ye regarding Joseph how he guarded himself from a woman, and purged his thoughts from all fornication, and found favour in the sight of Elohim (God) and men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:9: For the Egyptian woman did many things unto him, and summoned magicians, and offered him love potions, but the purpose of his soul admitted no evil desire.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:10: Therefore the Elohim (God) of your fathers delivered him from every evil (and) hidden death.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|4:11: For if fornication overcomes not your mind, neither can Beliar overcome you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:4: For a woman cannot force a man openly, but by a harlot's bearing she beguiles him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:1: For evil are women, my children; and since they have no power or strength over man, they use wiles by outward attractions that they may draw him to themselves.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:2: And whom they cannot bewitch by outward attractions, him they overcome by craft.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:3: For moreover, concerning them, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) told me, and taught me, that women are overcome by the spirit of fornication more than men, and in their heart they plot against men; and by means of their adornment they deceive first their minds, and by the glance of the eye instil the poison, and then through the accomplished act they take them captive.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:5: Flee, therefore, fornication, my children, and command your wives and your daughters, that they adorn not their heads and faces to deceive the mind; because every woman who useth these wiles hath been reserved for eternal punishment.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:6: For thus they allured the Watchers who were before the flood; for as these continually beheld them, they lusted after them, and they conceived the act in their mind; for they changed themselves into the shape of men, and appeared to them when they were with their husbands.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|5:7: And the women lusting in their minds after their forms, gave birth to giants, for the Watchers appeared to them as reaching even unto heaven.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:1: Beware, therefore, of fornication; and if you wish to be pure in mind, guard your senses from every woman.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:2: And command the women likewise not to associate with men, that they also may be pure in mind.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:3: For constant meetings, even though the ungodly deed be not wrought, are to them an irremediable disease, and to us a destruction of Beliar and an eternal reproach.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:4: For in fornication there is neither understanding nor godliness, and all jealousy dwelleth in the lust thereof.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:5: Therefore, then, I say unto you, ye will be jealous against the sons of Levi, and will seek to be exalted over them; but ye shall not be able.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:6: For Elohim (God) will avenge them, and ye shall die by an evil death.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:7: For to Levi Elohim (God) gave the sovereignty [and to Yahudah (Judah) with him and to me also, and to Dan and Joseph, that we should be for rulers].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:8: Therefore I command you to hearken to Levi, because he shall know the law of Yahuah (Lord), and shall give ordinances for judgment and shall sacrifice for all Yashar'el (Israel) until the consummation of the times, as the anointed High Priest, of whom Yahuah (Lord) spake.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:9: I adjure you by the Elohim (God) of heaven to do truth each one unto his neighbour and to entertain love each one for his brother.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:10: And draw ye near to Levi in humbleness of heart, that ye may receive a blessing from his mouth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:11: For he shall bless Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), because him hath Yahuah (Lord) chosen to be king over all the nation.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|6:12: And bow down before his seed, for on our behalf it will die in wars visible and invisible, and will be among you an eternal king.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|7:1: And Reuben died, having given these commands to his sons.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|7:2: And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|8:1: The copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph, his brother, died.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|8:2: For when Simeon was sick, his sons came to visit him, and he strengthened himself and sat up and kissed them, and said:—
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:1: Hearken, my children, to Simeon your father, And I will declare unto you what things I have in my heart.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:2: I was born of Jacob as my father's second son; And my mother Leah called me Simeon, Because Yahuah (Lord) had heard her prayer.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:3: Moreover, I became strong exceedingly; I shrank from no achievement, Nor was I afraid of ought.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:4: For my heart was hard, And my liver was immovable, And my bowels without compassion.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:5: Because valour also has been given from the El Elyon (Most High) to men in soul and body.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:6: For in the time of my youth I was jealous 'in many things' of Joseph, because my father loved him 'beyond all'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:7: And I set my mind against him to destroy him, because the prince of deceit sent forth the spirit of jealousy and blinded my mind, so that I regarded him not as a brother, nor did I spare even Jacob my father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:8: But his Elohim (God) and the Elohim (God) of his fathers sent forth His angel, and delivered him out of my hands.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:9: For when I went to Shechem to bring ointment for the flocks, and Reuben to Dothan, where were our necessaries and all our stores, Yahudah (Judah) my brother sold him to the Ishmaelites.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:10: And when Reuben heard these things he was grieved, for he wished to restore him to his father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:11: But on hearing this I was 'exceedingly' wroth against Yahudah (Judah) in that he let him go away alive, and for five months I continued wrathful against him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:12: But Yahuah (Lord) restrained me, and withheld 'from me' the power of my hands; for my right hand was half withered for seven days.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:13: And I knew, my children, that because of Joseph this had befallen me, and I repented and wept; and I besought Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) that my hand might be restored, and that I might hold aloof from all pollution and envy, 'and from all folly'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|9:14: For I knew that I had devised an evil thing before Yahuah (Lord) and Jacob my father, on account of Joseph my brother, in that I envied him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|10:1: And now, my children, 'hearken unto me and' beware of the spirit of deceit and of envy.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|10:2: For envy ruleth over the whole mind of a man, and suffereth him 'neither to eat nor to drink', nor to do any good thing.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|10:3: But it ever suggesteth (to him) to destroy him that he envieth; and so long as he that is envied flourisheth, he that envieth fadeth away.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|10:4: Two years 'therefore' I afflicted my soul with fasting in the fear of Yahuah (Lord), and I learnt that deliverance from envy cometh by the fear of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|10:5: For if a man flee to Yahuah (Lord), the evil spirit runneth away from him, and his mind is lightened.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|10:6: And henceforward he sympathiseth with him whom he envied and agreeth with those who love him, and so ceaseth from his envy.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:1: And my father asked 'concerning me', because he saw that I was sad; and I said unto him, I am pained in my liver.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:2: For I mourned more than they all, because I was guilty of the selling of Joseph.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:3: And when we went down into Egypt, and he bound me as a spy, I knew that I was suffering justly, and I grieved not.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:4: Now Joseph was a good man, and had the Spirit of Elohim (God) within him: being compassionate and pitiful, he bore no malice against me; but loved me even as the rest of his brethren.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:5: Beware, therefore, my children, of all jealousy and envy, and walk in singleness of heart, soul and with good heart, keeping in mind Joseph your father's brother, that Elohim (God) may give 'you also' grace and glory, and blessing upon your heads, even as ye saw in Joseph's case.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:6: All his days he reproached us not concerning this thing, but loved us as his own soul, and beyond his own sons glorified us, and gave us riches, and cattle and fruits.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:7: Do ye also, my children, love each one his brother with a good heart, and the spirit of envy will withdraw from you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:8: For this maketh savage the soul and destroyeth the body; it causeth anger and war in the mind, and stirreth up unto deeds of blood, and leadeth the mind into frenzy, 'and suffereth not prudence to act in men; moreover, it taketh away sleep', [and causeth tumult to the soul and trembling to the body].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|11:9: For even in sleep some malicious jealousy, deluding him, gnaweth, and with wicked spirits disturbeth his soul, and causeth the body to be troubled, and waketh the mind from sleep in confusion; and as a wicked and poisonous spirit, so appeareth it to men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|12:1: Therefore was Joseph comely in appearance, and goodly to look upon, because no wickedness dwelt in him; for some of the trouble of the spirit the face manifesteth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|12:2: And now, my children, Make your hearts good before Yahuah (Lord), And your ways straight before men, And ye shall find grace before Yahuah (Lord) and men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|12:3: Beware, therefore, of fornication, For fornication is mother of all evils, Separating from Elohim (God), and bringing near to Beliar.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|12:4: For I have seen it inscribed in the writing of Enoch that your sons shall be corrupted in fornication, and shall do harm to the sons of Levi with the sword.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|12:5: But they shall not be able to withstand Levi; for he shall wage the war of Yahuah (Lord), and shall conquer 'all' your hosts.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|12:6: And they shall be few in number, divided in Levi and Yahudah (Judah), and there shall be none of you for sovereignty, even as also our father prophesied in his blessings.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:1: Behold I have told you all things, that I may be acquitted of your sin.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:2: Now, if ye remove from you your envy and all stiff-neckedness, As a rose shall my bones flourish in Yashar'el (Israel), And as a lily my flesh in Jacob, And my odour shall be as the odour of Libanus; And as cedars shall holy ones be multiplied from me for ever, And their branches shall stretch afar off.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:3: Then shall perish the seed of Canaan, And a remnant shall not be unto Amalek, [And all the Cappadocians shall perish, And all the Hittites shall be utterly destroyed.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:4: Then shall fail the land of Ham, And all the people shall perish. Then shall all the earth rest from trouble, And all the world under heaven from war.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:5: Then the Mighty One of Yashar'el (Israel) shall glorify Shem, For Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) shall appear on earth, And save the sons of men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:6: Then shall all the spirits of deceit be given to be trodden under foot, And men shall rule over wicked spirits.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|13:7: Then shall I arise in joy, And will bless the El Elyon (Most High) because of His marvellous works, [Because Elohim (God) hath taken a body and eaten with men and saved men].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|14:1: And now, my children, obey Levi and Yahudah (Judah), and be not lifted up against these two tribes, for from them shall arise unto you the salvation of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|14:2: For Yahuah (Lord) shall raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Yahudah (Judah) as it were a King [Elohim (God) and man], He shall save all [the Gentiles and] the race of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|14:3: Therefore I give you these commands that ye also may command your children, that they may observe them throughout their generations.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|15:1: And when Simeon had made an end of commanding his sons, he slept with his fathers, being an hundred and twenty years old.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|15:2: And they laid him in a wooden coffin, to take up his bones to Hebron. And they took them up secretly during a war of the Egyptians.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|15:3: For the bones of Joseph the Egyptians guarded in the tombs of the Kings.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|15:4: For the sorcerers told them, that on the departure of the bones of Joseph there should be throughout all the land darkness and gloom, and an exceeding great plague to the Egyptians, so that even with a lamp a man should not recognise his brother.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|16:1: And the sons of Simeon bewailed their father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|16:2: And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|17:1: The copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained unto his sons, according to all that they should do, and what things should befall them until the day of judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|17:2: He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die. And when they were gathered together he said to them:
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:1: I, Levi, was born in Haran, and I came with my father to Shechem.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:2: And I was young, about twenty years of age, when, with Simeon, I wrought vengeance on Hamor for our sister Dinah.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:3: And when I was feeding the flocks in Abel-Maul, the spirit of understanding of Yahuah (Lord) came upon me, and I saw all men corrupting their way, and that unrighteousness had built for itself walls, and lawlessness sat upon towers.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:4: And I was grieving for the race of the sons of men, and I prayed to Yahuah (Lord) that I might be saved.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:5: Then there fell upon me a sleep, and I beheld a high mountain, and I was upon it.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:6: And behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:7: And I entered from the first heaven, and I saw there a great sea hanging.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:8: And further I saw a second heaven far brighter and more brilliant, for there was a boundless light also therein.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:9: And I said to the angel, Why is this so? And the angel said to me, Marvel not at this, for thou shalt see another heaven more brilliant and incomparable.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:10: And when thou hast ascended thither, Thou shalt stand near Yahuah (Lord), And shalt be His minister, And shalt declare His mysteries to men, And shalt proclaim concerning Him that shall redeem Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:11: And by thee and Yahudah (Judah) shall Yahuah (Lord) appear among men, [Saving every race of men].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|18:12: And from Yahuah's (Lord's) portion shall be thy life, And He shall be thy field and vineyard, And fruits, gold, and silver.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:1: Hear, therefore, regarding the heavens which have been shown to thee. The lowest is for this cause gloomy unto thee, in that it beholds all the unrighteous deeds of men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:2: And it has fire, snow, and ice made ready for the day of judgment, in the righteous judgment of Elohim (God); for in it are all the spirits of the retributions for vengeance on men.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:3: And in the second are the hosts of the armies which are ordained for the day of judgment, to work vengeance on the spirits of deceit and of Beliar. And above them are the holy ones.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:4: And in the highest of all dwelleth the Great Glory, far above all holiness.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:5: In [the heaven next to] it are the archangels, who minister and make propitiation to Yahuah (Lord) for all the sins of ignorance of the righteous;
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:6: Offering to Yahuah (Lord) a sweet-smelling savour, a reasonable and a bloodless offering.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:7: And [in the heaven below this] are the angels who bear answers to the angels of the presence of Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:8: And in [the heaven next to this] are thrones and dominions, in which always they offer praise to Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:9: When, therefore, Yahuah (Lord) looketh upon us, all of us are shaken; yea, the heavens, and the earth, and the abysses are shaken at the presence of His majesty.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|19:10: But the sons of men, having no perception of these things, sin and provoke the El Elyon (Most High).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|20:1: Now, therefore, know that Yahuah (Lord) shall execute judgment upon the sons of men. Because when the rocks are being rent, And the sun quenched, And the waters dried up, And the fire cowering, And all creation troubled, And the invisible spirits melting away, And Hades taketh spoils through the visitations of the El Elyon (Most High), Men will be unbelieving and persist in their iniquity. On this account with punishment shall they be judged.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|20:2: Therefore the El Elyon (Most High) hath heard thy prayer, To separate thee from iniquity, and that thou shouldest become to Him a son, And a servant, and a minister of His presence.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|20:3: The light of knowledge shalt thou light up in Jacob, And as the sun shalt thou be to all the seed of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|20:4: And there shall be given to thee a blessing, and to all thy seed, Until Yahuah (Lord) shall visit all the Gentiles in His tender mercies for ever.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|20:5: And therefore there have been given to thee counsel and understanding, That thou mightest instruct thy sons concerning this;
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|20:6: Because they that bless Him shall be blessed, And they that curse Him shall perish.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:1: And thereupon the angel opened to me the gates of heaven, and I saw the holy temple, and upon a throne of glory the El Elyon (Most High).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:2: And He said to me: Levi, I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:3: Then the angel brought me down to the earth, and gave me a shield and a sword, and said to me: Execute vengeance on Shechem because of Dinah, thy sister, and I will be with thee because Yahuah (Lord) hath sent me.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:4: And I destroyed at that time the sons of Hamor, as it is written in the heavenly tables.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:5: And I said to him: I pray Thee, O Yahuah (Lord), tell me Thy name, that I may call upon Thee in a day of tribulation.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:6: And he said: I am the angel who intercedeth for the nation of Yashar'el (Israel) that they may not be smitten utterly, for every evil spirit attacketh it.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|21:7: And after these things I awaked, and blessed the El Elyon (Most High), and the angel who intercedeth for the nation of Yashar'el (Israel) and for all the righteous.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:3: And I slew Shechem first, and Simeon slew Hamor.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:4: And after this my brothers came and smote that city with the edge of the sword.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:1: And when I was going to my father, I found a brazen shield; wherefore also the name of the mountain is Aspis, which is near Gebal, to the south of Abila.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:2: And I kept these words in my heart. And after this I counselled my father, and Reuben my brother, to bid the sons of Hamor not to be circumcised; for I was jealous because of the abomination which they had wrought on my sister.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:5: And my father heard these things and was wroth, and he was grieved in that they had received the circumcision, and after that had been put to death, and in his blessings he looked amiss upon us.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:6: For we sinned because we had done this thing against his will, and he was sick on that day.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:7: But I saw that the sentence of Elohim (God) was for evil upon Shechem; for they sought to do to Sarah and Rebecca as they had done to Dinah our sister, but Yahuah (Lord) prevented them.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:8: And they persecuted Abraham our father when he was a stranger, and they vexed his flocks when they were big with young; and Eblaen, who was born in his house, they most shamefully handled.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:9: And thus they did to all strangers, taking away their wives by force, and they banished them.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|22:10: But the wrath of Yahuah (Lord) came upon them to the uttermost.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|23:1: And I said to my father Jacob: By thee will Yahuah (Lord) destroy the Canaanites, and will give their land to thee and to thy seed after thee.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|23:2: For from this day forward shall Shechem be called a city of imbeciles; for as a man mocketh a fool, so did we mock them,
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|23:3: Because also they had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) by defiling my sister. And we departed and came to Bethel.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:18: And when I awoke, I understood that this (dream) was like the first dream.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:19: And I hid this also in my heart, and told it not to any man upon the earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:17: And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes; For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:1: And there again I saw a vision even as the former, after we had spent there seventy days.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:2: And I saw seven men in white raiment saying unto me: Arise, put on the robe of the priesthood, and the crown of righteousness, and the breastplate of understanding, and the garment of truth, and the plate of faith, and the turban of the head, and the ephod of prophecy.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:3: And they severally carried (these things) and put (them) on me, and said unto me: From henceforth become a priest of Yahuah (Lord), thou and thy seed for ever.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:4: And the first anointed me with holy oil, and gave to me the staff of judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:5: The second washed me with pure water, and fed me with bread and wine (even) the most holy things, and clad me with a holy and glorious robe.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:6: The third clothed me with a linen vestment like an ephod.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:7: The fourth put round me a girdle like unto purple.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:8: The fifth gave me a branch of rich olive.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:9: The sixth placed a crown on my head.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:10: The seventh placed on my head a diadem of priesthood, and filled my hands with incense, that I might serve as priest to Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:11: And they said to me: Levi, thy seed shall be divided into three offices, for a sign of the glory of Yahuah (Lord) who is to come.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:12: And the first portion shall be great; yea, greater than it shall none be.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:13: The second shall be in the priesthood.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:14: And the third shall be called by a new name, because a king shall arise in Yahudah (Judah), and shall establish a new priesthood, after the fashion of the Gentiles [to all the Gentiles].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:15: And His presence is beloved, as a prophet of the El Elyon (Most High), of the seed of Abraham our father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|24:16: Therefore, every desirable thing in Yashar'el (Israel) shall be for thee and for thy seed, And ye shall eat everything fair to look upon, And the table of Yahuah (Lord) shall thy seed apportion.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:1: And after two days I and Yahudah (Judah) went up with our father Jacob to Isaac our father's father.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:2: And my father's father blessed me according to all the words of the visions which I had seen. And he would not come with us to Bethel.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:3: And when we came to Bethel, my father Jacob saw a vision concerning me, that I should be their priest unto Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:4: And he rose up early in the morning, and paid tithes of all to Yahuah (Lord) through me.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:5: And so we came to Hebron to dwell there.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:6: And Isaac called me continually to put me in remembrance of the law of Yahuah (Lord), even as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) showed unto me.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:7: And he taught me the law of the priesthood, of sacrifices, whole burnt-offerings, first-fruits, freewill-offerings, peace-offerings.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:8: And each day he was instructing me, and was busied on my behalf before Yahuah (Lord), and said to me:
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:9: Beware of the spirit of fornication; for this shall continue and shall by thy seed pollute the holy place.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:10: Take, therefore, to thyself a wife without blemish or pollution, while yet thou art young, and not of the race of strange nations.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:11: And before entering into the holy place, bathe; and when thou offerest the sacrifice, wash; and again, when thou finishest the sacrifice, wash.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:12: Of twelve trees having leaves offer to Yahuah (Lord), as Abraham taught me also.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:13: And of every clean beast and bird offer a sacrifice to Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|25:14: And of all thy first-fruits and of wine offer the first, as a sacrifice to Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God); and every sacrifice thou shalt salt with salt.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|26:1: Now, therefore, observe whatsoever I command you, children; for whatsoever things I have heard from my fathers I have declared unto you.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|26:2: And behold, I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages [against the Saviour of the world, Messiah (Christ), acting godlessly], deceiving Yashar'el (Israel), and stirring up against it great evils from Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|26:3: And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|26:4: And ye shall be scattered as captives among the Gentiles, and shall be for a reproach and for a curse there.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|26:5: For the house which Yahuah (Lord) shall choose shall be called Jerusalem, as is contained in the book of Enoch the righteous.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:1: Therefore when I took a wife I was twenty-eight years old, and her name was Melcha.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:2: And she conceived and bare a son, and I called his name Gersam, for we were sojourners in our land.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:3: And I saw concerning him, that he would not be in the first rank.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:4: And Kohath was born in the thirty-fifth year of my life, towards sunrise.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:5: And I saw in a vision that he was standing on high in the midst of all the congregation.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:6: Therefore I called his name Kohath [which is, beginning of majesty and instruction].
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:7: And she bare me a third son, Merari, in the fortieth year of my life; and since his mother bare him with difficulty, I called him Merari, that is my bitterness, because he also was like to die.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|27:8: And Jochebed was born in Egypt, in my sixty-fourth year, for I was renowned then in the midst of my brethren.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:1: And Gersam took a wife, and she bare to him Lomni and Semei.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:2: And the sons of Kohath, Ambram, Issachar, Hebron, and Ozeel.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:3: And the sons of Merari, Mooli and Mouses.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:4: And in my ninety-fourth year Ambram took Jochebed my daughter to him to wife, for they were born in one day, he and my daughter.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:5: Eight years old was I when I went into the land of Canaan, and eighteen years when I slew Shechem, and at nineteen years I became priest, and at twenty-eight years I took a wife, and at forty-eight I went into Egypt.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:6: And behold, my children, ye are a third generation.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|28:7: In my hundred-and-eighteenth year Joseph died.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:1: And now, my children, I command you: Fear Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God) with your whole heart, And walk in simplicity according to all His law.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:2: And do ye also teach your children letters, That they may have understanding all their life, Reading unceasingly the law of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:3: For every one that knoweth the law of Yahuah (Lord) shall be honoured, And shall not be a stranger whithersoever he goeth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:4: Yea, many friends shall he gain more than his parents, And many men shall desire to serve him, And to hear the law from his mouth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:5: Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:6: And sow good things in your souls, That ye may find them in your life. But if ye sow evil things, Ye shall reap every trouble and affliction.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:7: Get wisdom in the fear of Elohim (God) with diligence; For though there be a leading into captivity, And cities and lands be destroyed, And gold and silver and every possession perish, The wisdom of the wise naught can take away, Save the blindness of ungodliness, and the callousness (that comes) of sin.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:8: For if one keep oneself from these evil things, Then even among his enemies shall wisdom be a glory to him, And in a strange country a fatherland, And in the midst of foes shall prove a friend.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|29:9: Whosoever teaches noble things and does them, Shall be enthroned with kings, As was also Joseph my brother.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|30:1: Therefore, my children, I have learnt that at the end of the ages ye will transgress against Yahuah (Lord), stretching out hands to wickedness [against Him]; and to all the Gentiles shall ye become a scorn.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|30:2: For our father Yashar'el (Israel) is pure from the transgressions of the chief priests [who shall lay their hands upon the Saviour of the world].
